translations.text: The Vision of the Prophet Ezekiel
In the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, I was among the exiles beside the River Chebar. The heavens opened, and I saw a vision of God.
On the fifth day of the month—it was the fifth year of King Jehoiachin’s exile—
the word of the Lord came to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans, by the River Chebar. There the hand of the Lord came upon me.

I looked, and there was a rising wind coming from the north, with a great cloud beside it. Fire flashed from it, and light surrounded it. Within it was something like the appearance of many-colored gems, with rays shining in it.
Within it were the forms of four living creatures. This was their appearance: they had a human form.
Each one had four faces, and each one of them had four wings.
Their thighs were straight, and their feet were winged. Their hooves were like calves’ hooves, and sparks shook loose from them like flashes of bronze. Their wings were swift.
A human hand was beneath their wings on their four sides. All four had faces and wings.
Their wings joined together, touching one another. As they moved, they did not turn their faces backward; each went straight ahead in the direction its faces faced.
The forms of their faces were a human face, a lion’s face on the right of all four, and an ox’s face and an eagle’s face on the left of all four.
These were their forms. The wings of all four were spread out above; each had two wings joined to one another, and two wings covering their bodies from above.
Each went straight ahead in the direction its faces faced. They went wherever the wind headed, and they did not turn backward as they moved.
Among the creatures was something like the appearance of burning coals of fire, and like lamps mingled among the creatures. The fire was bright, and flashes of lightning burst from the fire.
The creatures ran swiftly and turned lightly, like the sun.
I looked, and there was a wheel on the ground beside the four creatures.

The appearance of the wheels and their workmanship were like the appearance of gems from Tarshish. All four had the same form, and their appearance and construction were as though a wheel were turning within a wheel.
They moved toward their four sides and did not turn backward behind them.
They were high. I looked at them and saw that their rims were full of eyes all around all four.
When the creatures moved, the wheels moved with them, and when the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels also rose.
Wherever the cloud and the wind headed, the creatures went, and the wheels rose with them, because a living spirit was in the wheels.
When they moved, the wheels moved; when they stood still, the wheels stayed in place. When they rose from the ground, the wheels rose with them, because a living spirit was in the wheels.
Above the creatures’ heads was the likeness of a firmament, like the appearance of a crystal stone, spread out above their wings.
Beneath the firmament, their wings were spread out, hovering toward one another, and each had two wings covering its body.

I heard the sound of their wings as they hovered, like the sound of many waters and like the voice of God Shaddai. As they moved, there was a sound of proclamations, like the sound of an army; when they stood still, their wings rested.
And behold, a voice came from above the firmament that was over their heads, as they stood still and raised their wings.
And above the firmament that was over their heads was something resembling a sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne upon it; and upon the throne was a likeness in human form.

And I saw something like a multicolored stone, like the appearance of fire beneath it all around. From the waist upward it resembled the sun, and from the waist downward it resembled fire; and the light around it formed a halo.

It was like the appearance of the rainbow that stretches across the clouds on rainy days, and so was the awesome appearance of the light around it. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord. When I saw it, I fell on my face and heard a voice speaking to me.
And he said, “Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak to you.”
And the Spirit came upon me, lifted me up, and set me standing on my feet; and I heard him speaking to me.
And he said, “Son of man, I will send you to the rebellious house of Israel, who have provoked me. They and their fathers have dishonored me to this very day.
The children to whom I am sending you are insolent and hardhearted. You shall say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord God.’
Whether they listen or tremble—for they are a rebellious house—they will at least know that you are a prophet among them.

And you, son of man, do not fear them or be dismayed before them, for they will become fiercely angry and rise up against you, and you dwell among scorpions. Do not fear their words or be dismayed before them, for they are a rebellious house.
And you shall speak these words to them, whether they listen or tremble, for they are a rebellious house.
And you, son of man, listen to the words I speak to you. Do not be rebellious like the rebellious house. Open your mouth and eat what I will give you.”
I looked, and behold, a hand was stretched out toward me, and in it was a written scroll. He unrolled it before me, and written on it, inside and outside, were lamentations, cries, and woes.
And he said to me, “Son of man, eat whatever you find in it. Eat this scroll completely, and go and speak to the children of Israel.”
He opened my mouth and gave me the scroll.
And he said to me, “Son of man, let your mouth eat and your belly be filled with this scroll that was given to you.” I ate it, and in my mouth it was like the sweetness of honey.
And he said to me, “Son of man, go and enter the house of Israel, and speak my messages to them.
For you are not being sent to a people whose speech is obscure and whose language is difficult, but to the house of Israel,

and not to many peoples of foreign nations or foreign languages, nor to those whose language is difficult, whose words you cannot understand. For if I sent you to such people, even they would listen to you.
But the house of Israel is unwilling to listen to you, because they do not want to listen to me; for the whole house of Israel is defiant and hardhearted.
And behold, I have made your face firm before their faces, and I will strengthen your resolve against their opposition.
And your resolve shall always be firm as a rock. Do not fear them or be dismayed before them, for they are a rebellious house.”
And the Lord said to me, “Son of man, hear with your ears all the words I have spoken to you, and lay them in your heart.
And go, enter among the exiles, among the children of your people. Speak to them and say, ‘Thus says the Lord God,’ whether they listen and heed.”
And the Spirit lifted me up, and behind me I heard the sound of a great shaking, as they said, “Blessed be the glory of the Lord from his place!”
And I saw the sound of the wings of the living creatures fluttering against one another, and the sound of the wheels behind them, and the sound of movement.
And the Spirit of the Lord lifted me up and raised me, and I went, lifted up by the impulse of my spirit, and the hand of the Lord was upon me with power.
And I entered, lifted up, among the exiles and went about among the inhabitants by the River Chebar who were there, and I sat quietly among them for seven days.
And after seven days, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, I have appointed you a watchman for the house of Israel. You shall hear messages from me and warn them as from me.

When I say to the wicked person, ‘You shall surely die,’ and you do not warn him or speak to warn the wicked person to turn from his evil ways and live, that wicked person shall die in his wickedness, and I will require his blood from your hands.
But if you warn the wicked person and he does not turn from his wickedness and his way, that wicked person shall die in his wickedness, but you shall save your own life.

And when a righteous person turns from his righteous deeds and commits transgressions, I will bring punishments upon his head, and he shall die, for the righteous deeds he has done shall not be remembered. But because you did not warn him, I will require his blood from your hands.
But if you warn the righteous person not to sin, the righteous person shall surely live because you warned him, and you shall save your own life.
And the hand of the Lord was upon me there, and he said to me, ‘Rise and go out into the plain, and there I will speak with you.’

I rose and went out into the plain, and behold, the glory of the Lord had descended and stood there, like the vision and the glory that I had seen on the bank of the River Chebar, and I fell on my face.
And the Spirit came upon me and set me on my feet, and he spoke with me and said, ‘Go in and shut yourself inside your house.’
And you, son of man, behold, bonds have been placed upon you, and they shall bind you with them, and you shall not go out from among them.
And I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, and you will be mute and will not be a man who rebukes them, for they are a rebellious house.

And when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you shall say to them, ‘Thus says Adonai, Lord, Lord: Let whoever will listen listen, and let whoever will disregard it disregard it, for they are a rebellious house.’
And you, son of man, take a brick for yourself, place it before you, and draw the city of Jerusalem on it.
And lay siege around it, build siege towers around it, surround it with a rampart, set up camps around it, and bring catapults all around it.

And take an iron pan for yourself and set it up as an iron wall between you and the city. Direct your face against it, and it shall be under siege, and you shall besiege it, for this is a sign to the children of Israel.

And you shall lie on your left side and place the iniquities of the house of Israel upon it. According to the number of days you lie on it, one hundred and fifty days, you shall bear their iniquities.
And I have assigned you their two iniquities as a number of days, one hundred and ninety days, and you shall bear the iniquities of the house of Israel.
And you shall complete them all together, and again you shall lie on your right side and bear the iniquity of the house of Judah for forty days, for I have assigned you one day for each year.
And you shall set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, strengthen your arms, and prophesy against it.
And behold, I have placed bonds upon you, and you shall not turn from one side to the other until the days of your confinement are completed.

And you, take wheat and barley, lentils and peas, millet and spelt for yourself, and put them into one earthenware vessel and make bread from them for yourself. You shall eat it according to the number of days you lie on your side, one hundred and ninety days.
You shall eat your food by weight, twenty shekels a day; you shall eat some of it from time to time.
And you shall drink water by measure, one-sixth of a jar; you shall drink it from time to time.
You shall eat some of it as a barley cake; bake it over human dung before their eyes.
And you shall say, “Thus says the Lord God of Israel: In this way the children of Israel shall eat their bread in uncleanness among the nations where I shall scatter them.”

And I said, “Far be it, Lord God of Israel, that I should ever have defiled myself with unclean things! From my birth until now, I have never eaten anything that died on its own or was torn by wild beasts, nor has any unclean meat entered my mouth.”
And he said to me, “Look, I have given you cattle dung instead of human dung, and with it you shall make your bread.”
And the Lord said to me, “Son of man, look, I am breaking the supply of bread in Jerusalem. They shall eat bread by weight and in want, and drink water by measure and in need,
so that they shall lack bread and water, and a man and his brother shall waste away, and they shall wither away in their wrongdoing.”

And you, son of man, take for yourself a sword sharpened on a whetstone, sharper than a barber’s razor. Get it for yourself and pass it over your head and your beard. Then take scales and weigh the hair.

Burn one-fourth in the fire in the middle of the city when the days of the siege are completed. Cut up one-fourth with the sword around it, and scatter one-fourth to the wind; and I shall send a sword after it.
And take a small number of hairs from it and bind them in your cloak.
Then take some of these again, throw them into the fire, and burn them in the fire. From there a fire shall come out, and you shall say to the whole house of Israel:
“Thus says Adonai, the Lord: This is Jerusalem, which I placed among the nations, with lands all around her.
For they exchanged my judgments for the wickedness of the nations, and my laws for the laws of the lands around her, because they rejected my judgments and did not walk in my laws.

Therefore thus says Adonai, the Lord: Because your impulses come from the nations around you, and you have not walked in my laws or carried out my judgments, nor have you even acted according to the judgments of the nations around you,
therefore thus says Adonai, the Lord: Look, I am against you, and I shall carry out judgment in your midst before the nations.
And I shall do to you what I have never done before, and will never do anything like again, because of all your abominations.
Therefore fathers shall eat their sons in your midst, and sons shall eat their fathers. I shall carry out judgments against you and scatter all your survivors to every wind.

Therefore, as I live, says Adonai, the Lord, because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your detestable things and all your unclean acts of worship, I too shall reject you. My eye shall not spare you, and I shall not have mercy on you.

One-fourth of you shall be consumed by death, and one-fourth of you shall perish by famine in your midst. One-fourth of you shall fall by the sword around you, and one-fourth of you I shall scatter to every wind, and I shall send a sword after them.
And the fury of my anger against them shall be fulfilled, and I shall be comforted. They shall know that I, the Lord, have spoken in my jealousy, when I have fully poured out my anger upon them.
And I shall make you a wasteland and a reproach among the nations around you, and your daughters around you, before everyone who passes along the road.

And you shall become an object of lamentation and pity, a mockery and a spectacle among the nations around you, when I carry out judgments against you in anger, fury, and wrathful vengeance. I, the Lord, have spoken.
When I send my dreadful arrows of famine against them, they shall bring destruction. I shall send this against them, and I shall heap famine upon you and break your supply of bread.

And I will send famine and vicious beasts against you, and I will punish you. Death and bloodshed will pass through you, and I will bring a sword against you on every side, for I, the Lord, have spoken.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, set your face against the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them.

And say: Mountains of Israel, hear the words of the Lord God. This is what the Lord God says to the mountains and hills, the valleys and plains: Look, I am bringing a sword against you, and your high places will be destroyed.
Your altars will be demolished, and your shrines will be shattered, and I will lay your slain before your idols.
And I will lay the corpses of the Israelites strewn before your images, and I will scatter your bones around your altars.

Throughout all your settlements, the cities will be devastated and the high places destroyed, so that your altars will be obliterated and cease to exist, your idols will be shattered and come to an end, your shrines will be removed, and the works of your hands will be wiped out.
And the slain will fall among you, and you will know that I am the Lord.
And I will leave some of you alive, survivors of the sword among the nations, when you are scattered among the lands.

And your survivors will remember me among the nations where they were taken captive, for I swore against their adulterous hearts, which rebelled against me, and against their eyes, which lustfully followed their own ways. And they will beat their faces in mourning because of the evil they committed in all their detestable practices and in all their ways.
And they will know that I am the Lord, and that I did not speak in vain when I said I would bring all these calamities upon them.

This is what the Lord God says: Clap your hands and stamp your foot, and say, ‘Alas, alas for the detestable practices and the evil deeds of the house of Israel!’ For they will fall by sword, death, and famine.
Those far away will die of death, those nearby will fall by the sword, and those who remain and are besieged will perish from famine. And I will fully unleash my anger upon them.

And they will know that I am the Lord when your slain fall among your idols, around your altars, on every high hill and every mountaintop, beneath every leafy tree and beneath every sturdy oak, where they offered incense to all their idols.

And I will stretch out my hand against them and make the land a place of devastation and destruction, from the wilderness of Diblathah throughout all their settlements. And you will know that I am the Lord.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
And you, son of man, shall say: This is what the Lord God says to the land of the Israelites: The end has come! The end has come upon the four corners of the land.
Look, the end has come upon you, and I will send my wrath against you and judge you according to your ways, and repay you for all your detestable practices.
My eye will not spare you, and I will not have mercy, for I will repay you according to your ways, and your detestable practices will be in your midst. And you will know that I am the Lord.
For this is what the Lord God says: A calamity—look, a calamity has come!
The end has come; it has awakened against you. Look, it has come!
[?] is upon you, you who live in the land. The time has come, the day has drawn near, and not with tumult or with labor pains.
But now, very soon, I will pour out my anger upon you and fully unleash my wrath against you. I will judge you according to your ways and bring upon you all the defilement of your worship.

My eye shall not spare you, and I will no longer have mercy, for I will repay you according to your ways, and your detestable practices will be in your midst. And you will know that I am the Lord who strikes you.
Look, the day of the Lord! Look, the end has come! The [?] has come, the rod has blossomed, arrogance has arisen.
And you will shatter the strength of the lawless one, not with tumult and not with haste. They are not in their right minds, and there is no beauty in them.
The time has arrived; look, the day has come. Let the buyer not rejoice, and let the seller not mourn, for wrath is upon their entire multitude.

For the buyer will not return to the seller, nor will they continue living their lives, for the vision concerning their entire multitude will not turn back, and no man will stand firm in the sight of his own life.
Sound the trumpet and prepare everything, but let no one go to war, for wrath is upon their multitude.
The battle of the sword is outside, and famine and death are inside. Those who are outside will perish by the sword, and those who are in the city will perish by famine and death.
Those among them who are to escape will escape, and they will be on the mountains like doves, moaning without ceasing. I will kill them all, each one in his own lawlessness.
All hands will grow weak, and all loins will be fouled with wetness.
They shall put on sackcloth, and terrors shall cover them. Shame shall be on every face, and baldness on every head.

Their silver will lie fallen in the public squares, and their gold will be despised. Their silver and their gold will not be able to save them on the day of the Lord’s wrath. Their souls will not be satisfied, and their bellies will not be filled, for these have become torments for their injustice.
They made their very choicest ornaments a source of pride, and from them they made images for their abominable worship. Therefore I will make these a defilement to them.
And I will hand them over to foreigners to plunder them, and to the evildoers of the earth as spoil, and they will defile them.
I will turn my face away from them, and they will defile my visitation. They will enter them indiscriminately and defile them.
And they will make confusion, for the land is filled with judgments concerning their bloodshed, and the cities are full of lawlessness.
I will bring the wicked among the nations, and they will take possession of their houses. I will overthrow the arrogance of their oppression, and their holy places will be defiled.
Atonement will come, and they will seek peace, but it will not be found.
Woe will come upon woe, and bad news upon bad news. They will seek visions from the prophets, comforting laws from the priest, and counsel from the elders, but these will not be found.

The king will mourn, and the ruler will clothe himself in destruction, and the hands of the people of the land will grow weak. I will deal with them according to their ways, and according to their judgments I will exact vengeance from them, and they will know that I am the Lord.
In the sixth year, in the fifth month, on the fifth day of the month, I was sitting in my house, and the elders of Judah were sitting before me. There the hand of Adonai the Lord came upon me.

I looked, and there was the likeness of a man: from his waist downward there was fire, and from his waist upward there was something like the appearance of air, like the color of a multicolored gemstone.

He stretched out something like a hand and seized me by the crown of my head. The Spirit lifted me up between heaven and earth and brought me to Jerusalem in the vision of God. He set me at the entrance of the inner gate facing north, where the pillar of the image that provokes jealousy stood.
There was the glory of the God of Israel, like the vision that I had seen there in the plain.

He said to me, “Son of man, look with your eyes toward the north.” I lifted my eyes toward the north, and there, on the north side, above the gate of the altar, stood the image of jealousy at the entrance of the gate facing east.
He said to me, “Son of man, do you see what they are doing here—the great lawlessness of this house of Israel, departing from my holy places? You will yet see acts of lawlessness greater than these.”
He brought me before the doors of the portico, and I looked, and there was a hole in the wall.
He said to me, “Son of man, dig through that wall.” I dug through the wall, and there was a door.
And he said to me, “Son of man, go in and see the lawless acts and the evils that they commit there.”
I went in and saw, and there was every likeness of creeping things and animals, worthless abominations; and I saw all the idols of the house of Israel painted all around them.

And seventy men from among the elders of the house of Israel, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them, stood before them. Each had a censer in his hand, and the smoke of the incense rose and gathered like a cloud.

And the Lord said to me, “Son of man, do you see what the elders of the house of Israel are doing there in the darkness, each secretly in his own chamber? For they say, ‘The Lord has abandoned us and does not look upon the earth.’”
And he said to me, “You will see still greater lawless acts that they commit.”
And he brought me before the gate of the house of the Lord that faced north, and there were women sitting there, mourning Tammuz.
And he said to me, “Do you see this, son of man? You will see still greater deeds than these.”

And he brought me into the inner court of the house of the Lord. There, at the entrance of the Lord’s temple, between the altar and the railing, were about twenty-five men. Their backs were turned toward the Lord’s temple and their faces toward the east, and they were bowing down to the sun.

And he said to me, “Have you seen this, son of man? Is the lawlessness that the house of Israel commits here a small thing? They have filled the land with lawless acts and have turned to provoking me to anger. And now they stretch out a vine branch in contempt.”
And I will deal with them in anger. My eye will not spare them, and I will not have mercy on them. They will cry loudly in my ears, but I will not listen to them.
And he cried loudly in my ears and said, “The punishment of this city is near.” And each man had an instrument of destruction in his hand.

And there were six men coming along the road from the upper gate that faced north, each with an axe in his hand. Among them was a man dressed in a robe reaching to his feet, with a belt set with sapphire stones around his waist. They entered and stood before the bronze altar.

And the glory of the God of Israel rose from the cherubim into the open space in the middle of the temple. And he called the man who was dressed in the robe reaching to his feet and had the belt around his waist.
And the Lord said to him, “Pass through the middle of this city, Jerusalem, and put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and groan over the lawless acts committed among them.”
And he said to the others in my hearing, “Go after him into the city and slaughter. Let your eyes spare no one, and show no mercy.

Kill the old men and the children, the virgins and the young men, and the women, utterly destroying them. But do not approach anyone who has the mark on him. Begin with my sanctuary.” And they began with the elderly men who were inside the temple.
And he said to them, “Defile the house and fill the house with corpses, and go out.” And they went out and slaughtered the city.

And while they were slaughtering them, I looked and saw, and I fell on my face and cried out, saying, “Alas for me, Adonai, Lord! Will you wipe out that remnant of the house of Israel as you pour out your wrath upon Jerusalem?”

And he said to me, “The wrongdoing of the house of Israel and Judah has become very, very great, for the land has been filled with many peoples, and the city has become full of lawlessness and defilement. For they said, ‘The Lord has abandoned the land, and the Lord no longer looks upon it.’
And now my eye will not spare them, and I will not have mercy. Instead, I will bring their ways down upon their own heads.”
And the man who was dressed in the robe reaching to his feet and had the belt around his waist answered and said, “I have done as you commanded me.”
And I looked, and there, above the expanse over the heads of the cherubim, was something like a sapphire stone, and above them was the likeness of a throne.

And he said to the man dressed in the robe, “Go in among the wheels beneath the cherubim, fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim, and scatter them over the city.” And he went in before my eyes.
And the cherubim stood on the right side of the temple when the man entered, and the cloud filled the inner court.
And the glory of the Lord rose from the cherubim into the open space in the temple. The temple was filled with a cloud, and the court was filled with the light of the Lord’s glory.
And the sound of the cherubim’s wings could be heard as far as the outer court, like the voice of God Shaddai when he speaks.
While he was giving instructions to the man wearing the holy robe, saying, “Take fire from among the wheels, from among the cherubim,” the man went in and stood among the wheels.

One cherub stretched out his hand from among the cherubim into the fire that was among the cherubim. He took some and put it into the hands of the man wearing the holy robe, who took it and went out from there.
I looked at the cherubim and saw the likeness of human hands beneath their wings.
I looked, and there were four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside each cherub. The appearance of the wheels was like that of a carbuncle stone.
The appearance and likeness of all four were as though a wheel could be seen within a wheel.
When they moved, they went in any of their four directions and did not turn back, for they followed in whatever direction the one in front faced, and they did not turn back.
And their whole bodies, their hands, their wings, and the wheels were full of eyes all around their four wheels.
The wheels were called “Galgal” in my own hearing.
Each had four faces: the first face was the face of a cherub, the second the face of a human being, the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle.
The cherubim rose. This was the creature I had seen by the River Chebar.
When the cherubim moved, the wheels also moved after them. When the cherubim lifted their wings to rise from the earth, the wheels did not turn back, for they were following them.
When they stood still, the wheels stopped, and when they rose, the wheels rose with them, for the spirit of life was in them.
The glory of the Lord went out from the courtyard of the temple and rested upon the cherubim.

The cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the earth before me as they went out, with the wheels following them. They stood before the doorposts of the gate of the Lord’s house that faced east, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
This was the living creature I had seen beneath the God of Israel by the River Chebar, and I knew that they were cherubim.
Each had four faces and each had eight wings, with the likeness of human hands beneath their wings.

As for the likeness of their faces, these were the faces I had seen beneath the glory of the God of Israel by the River Chebar—their appearance and the creatures themselves. Each moved in the direction of its own face.

The Spirit lifted me up and brought me before the gate of the Lord’s house that faced east. There, before the gate of the portico, were about twenty-five men. Among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, leaders of the people.
The Lord said to me, “Son of man, these are the men who devise futile things and give evil counsel in that city.
They say, ‘Have not these houses been built recently? This city is the cauldron, and we are the meat.’
Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man.”
The Spirit of the Lord came upon me and said to me, “Thus says the Lord God: This is what you say, house of Israel, and I know the thoughts of your spirits.
Multiply your corpses in that city, and fill its roads with the wounded.
Therefore thus says the Lord God: The bodies of those you killed within this city are the meat, and it is the cauldron; but I will bring you out of it.
You feared the sword; I will bring a sword upon you, says the Lord God.
I will bring you out of it and hand you over to foreigners, and I will execute judgment upon you,
for you will fall by the sword. I will judge you on the mountains of Israel, and you will know that I am the Lord.”
And this shall not be a pot for you, nor shall you be meat in it. I will judge you on the mountains of Israel.
And you shall know that I am the LORD, because you did not walk according to my righteous decrees or carry out my judgments, but acted according to the customs of the nations around you.

And while I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. I fell on my face and cried out with a loud voice, saying, “Alas for me, alas for me, Lord GOD! You have brought the remnant of Israel to an end!”
The word of the Lord came to me and said:

Son of man, your brothers, the men of your captivity, and your entire house of Israel have come to an end. The inhabitants of Jerusalem said to them, “You have been cast far away from the LORD, for this land has been given to us as an inheritance.”
Therefore say, “Thus says the Lord GOD: Though I cast them away among the nations and scatter them throughout every land, I will be a small sanctuary for them in the regions into which they go.”
Therefore say, “Thus says the Lord GOD: I will receive them from the nations and gather them from the regions where I scatter them, and I will give them the land of Israel.”
And they shall enter there and remove all its abominations and all its lawlessness from it.
And I will give them a different heart and grant them a new spirit. I will remove the heart of stone from their bodies and give them a heart of flesh,
so that they may walk according to my commandments, keep my judgments, and carry them out. They shall be my people, and I will be their God.

And according to the abominations of their hearts, according to the lawless deeds they committed, and according to the ways in which they walked, I will repay them upon their heads, says the Lord GOD.
And the cherubim raised their wings, and the wheels followed them, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
And the glory of the LORD rose from the midst of the city and stood upon the mountain facing the city.
And the Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the land of the Chaldeans, among the captives, in a vision through the Spirit of God. And I came out of the vision that I had seen.
And I spoke to the captives all the words of the LORD that he had shown me.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, you dwell amid their lawlessness. They have eyes to see but do not see, and ears to hear but do not hear, because they are a rebellious house.

And you, son of man, prepare yourself equipment for exile, and go into exile by day before them. You shall go into exile from your own place to another place before them, so that they may see, for they are a rebellious house.
And you shall lay out your belongings like the belongings of an exile before their eyes, and you shall go out in the evening before them, as a captive goes out.
Before their eyes, make a hole for yourself in the wall and go out through it.
Before them you shall walk bent over and go out stealthily. You shall wrap a cloth around your head and not look at the land, for I have made you a sign to the house of Israel.

And I did everything as the LORD commanded me. I put out the belongings of an exile during the day, and in the evening I dug through the wall with my own hand. I went stealthily, bent over, before them.
And in the morning the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, has not the house of Israel, the rebellious house, said to you, ‘What is this that you are doing?’”
And now say to them, “Thus says the Lord GOD to these princes and leaders of Jerusalem and to the entire house of Israel who are among them:
‘I will make a sign in its midst. As you have done, so shall it happen to it, for they shall go into exile and captivity.
And the prince among them shall walk bent over and move stealthily. He shall break through the wall and go out, walking with his face covered, and he shall not see the land.
And I will cast my net over him, and he shall be enclosed in a net during the siege. I will bring him to Babylon, to the land of the Chaldeans, but he shall not see it, and there he shall die.’”
I will scatter all his helpers who are around him and all his defenders to every wind, and I will send a sword after them.
They will know that I am the Lord when I scatter them among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands.
I will spare a few of their men from famine, the sword, and death, so that they may recount all their lawless deeds among the nations to which they go. And they will know that I am the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, eat your bread in deprivation, and drink your water in torment and distress.

Say to the people of the land: Thus says the Lord God to the inhabitants of Jerusalem in the land of Israel: They will eat their bread in deprivation and drink their water in desolation, so that the land and everything in it may be laid waste, because all its inhabitants are wicked.
Their inhabited cities will be devastated, and their land will become a wasteland. And you will know that I am the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, what is this proverb you have in the land of Israel, which says, “The days are far off, and every vision has perished”?

Therefore say to them: Thus says the Lord God: I will put an end to that proverb, and the house of Israel will no longer repeat that proverb. You shall tell them: The days have arrived, and so have the pronouncements of every vision.
For there will no longer be any false vision or anyone who speaks flattering things through divination among the children of Israel.
For I, the Lord, have spoken my words; I have spoken, and I will act, and I will delay no longer. For in your days, rebellious house, I have spoken the word and will carry it out, says the Lord God.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, look: the house of Israel, the rebellious house, says, ‘The vision he sees is for many days from now, and what he prophesies will happen in distant times.’
Therefore say to them: Thus says the Lord God: None of the words I speak will be delayed any longer. Rather, whatever I speak, I will carry out, says the Lord God.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who prophesy there, and speak to those prophets who prophesy from their own hearts. Prophesy and say to them: Hear the pronouncements of the Lord.
Thus says the Lord God: Woe to those who prophesy from their own hearts, who follow their own spirits and see nothing at all!
Your prophets, Israel, were like foxes among ruins.
They did not stand firm, and they gathered flocks against the house of Israel. Those who spoke in the Lord’s name did not stand firm.
They saw falsehood and reported worthless divination, saying, ‘Thus says the Lord,’ though I, the Lord, had not sent them. And they began to establish their words.
Have you not seen false visions and recounted worthless divinations, saying, “Thus says the Lord,” when I, the Lord, have not spoken?
Therefore say: Thus says the Lord God: Because your words are false and your divinations are worthless, I am against you, says the Lord God.

And I will stretch out my hand against the prophets who saw falsehoods and spoke worthless things. They shall not stand in the council of my people, nor shall they be recorded in the register of the house of Israel, nor shall they enter the land of Israel. And they shall know that I am the Lord GOD.
Because they misled my people and said, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there was no peace, and he was building a wall while they plastered it so that it would collapse,

say to those who plastered it: That is foolishness, for it is going to collapse. Rain will come and flood it, and I will hurl stones against their joints, and they will be brought down. A wind will rise and overthrow it.
And look, the wall has collapsed! Will they not then say to you, ‘Where is the plaster with which you plastered it?’

For thus says the Lord God: I will unleash a wind that will sweep it away in my fury. Rain will come to flood it in my anger, and in wrath I will bring stones hurled as missiles against it, to destroy it completely.

I will demolish the wall you plastered, and it will collapse. I will cast it to the ground, and its foundations will be exposed. It will fall and come to an end under rebuke. And you will know that I am the Lord.
And I will vent my anger on the wall and on those who plaster it, and it will collapse. And I will say to you, ‘The wall is nowhere to be found, nor are those who plastered it—’
the prophets of Israel who prophesied about Jerusalem and saw peace for her, when there was no peace, says Adonai the Lord.
And you, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy from their own hearts, and prophesy against them.

And you shall say: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Woe to those who sew and stitch cushions beneath every elbow and make head coverings for heads of every height, to lead souls astray! For the souls of my people were led astray, and they bewildered souls.

And they maligned me before my people for a handful of barley and a piece of bread, killing souls who did not deserve to die and keeping alive souls who ought not to live, as you spoke into the ears of the people who delight in empty words.
Therefore, thus says the Lord, the Lord: Look, I am against your cushions, with which you gathered souls. I will tear them from your arms and release the souls whom you led astray, scattering them.
And I will tear your head coverings and rescue my people from your hands. They will no longer be in your hands to be gathered, and you will know that I am the Lord.

Because you unjustly led the heart of the righteous astray, though I had not led him astray, and strengthened the hands of the lawless, so that he would not turn at all from his lawlessness and his evil ways and live,
therefore you shall no longer see false visions or practice divination. And I will rescue my people from your hands, and you will know that I am the Lord.
And men from among the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, these men have set their thoughts in their hearts and placed the torments of their wrongdoing before their faces. Am I really to give them an answer?

Therefore, speak to them and say: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Any man of the house of Israel who sets his thoughts in his heart and places the punishment for his wrongdoing before his eyes, and comes to a prophet to inquire of me through him—I, the Lord, will answer him according to what he has in mind.
This is so that they may not lead the house of Israel astray according to their hearts, which have become estranged from me through their conduct.
Therefore, say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord, the Lord God: Turn back and turn away from your ways and from all your impieties, and turn your faces toward me.

For any man of the house of Israel, or of the newcomers and foreigners in Israel, who becomes estranged from me and sets his thoughts in his heart and places the punishment for his wrongdoing before his face, and comes to a prophet to inquire of me through him—I, the Lord, will answer him according to what he has in mind.
And I will set my face against that man. I will make him a sign and a ruin, and remove him from among my people. And you will know that I am the Lord.
And if a prophet is deceived and speaks a word, I, the Lord, have led that prophet astray. And I will stretch out my hand against him and destroy him from among my people Israel.
And they will bear their wrongdoing. The wrongdoing of the prophet will be like the wrongdoing of the one who inquires.
This is so that the house of Israel may no longer stray from me or defile themselves with any of their transgressions. They will be my people, and I will be their God, says Adonai the Lord.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, if a land sins against me by committing a transgression, I will stretch out my hand against it, break its supply of bread, send famine upon it, and remove people and animals from it.
And if those three men—Noah, Job, and Daniel—are in its midst, they will be saved by their righteousness, says Adonai the Lord.
And if I bring evil beasts upon the land and punish it, and it becomes a wasteland, so that no one can pass through it because of the beasts,
and those men are in it, as I live, says Adonai the Lord, their sons and daughters will not survive. Only they themselves will survive, and the land will be destroyed.
And if I bring a sword upon that land and command the sword to pass through the land, and remove humans and animals from it,
and those three men are in it, as I live, says Adonai the Lord, they will not save sons or daughters. Only they themselves will survive.
And if I send death into that land and pour out my wrath upon it in blood, to destroy humans and animals from it,
and Noah, Daniel, and Job are in it, as I live, says Adonai the Lord, their sons and daughters will not remain alive. But by their righteousness they will save their own lives.
Thus says Adonai the Lord: Even if I unleash all four terrible punishments—sword, famine, evil beasts, and death—upon Jerusalem, to destroy humans and animals from it,

the [?] survivors in it will bring out their sons and daughters. Look, they will come out to you with them, and you will see their ways and their thoughts, and you will relent concerning the disasters I brought upon Jerusalem, all the disasters I brought upon it.
And they will comfort you, because you will see their ways and their thoughts, and you will understand that I did not do without cause everything I did to them, says Adonai the Lord.
Concerning the wood of the vine
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, what is the wood of the vine compared with all the wood of the branches among the trees of the forest?
Do people take wood from it to make anything, or take a peg from it to hang a vessel on?
But it has been given to the fire to be consumed, for year after year the fire consumes its [?], and it dwindles away completely. Can it be useful for any work?
Even if it is cut down whole, it is of no use for any work. But if it becomes food for the fire entirely, it is of absolutely no use for any work.
Therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: Just as I gave the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest as food for the fire, so I will give up the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
And I will set my face against them. They will come out of the fire, and fire will devour them. And they will know that I am the Lord when I set my face against them.
And I will make the land a desolation because they fell into transgressions, says the Lord GOD.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, bear witness against Jerusalem concerning its lawlessness.
And you shall say: Thus says Adonai the Lord to Jerusalem: Your root and your birth are from the land of the Canaanites. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother a Hittite.

As for your birth, on the day you were born no one cut your umbilical cord, and your breasts were not bound. You were not washed with water for your preservation, nor rubbed with salt, nor wrapped in swaddling cloths.

And my eye did not pity you, and I did not do any of these things for you, taking care lest anything happen to you. You lay cast out upon the open field because of your crooked thoughts on the day you were born.
I passed by you and saw you drenched in blood, and I said to you: Live from your blood, and your life is from blood.

Multiply, for I made you like a plant of the field. And you multiplied and grew, and you came and entered the cities of cities. Your breasts drooped and your hair grew, but you were naked and exposed.

And I came to you and saw that your time had arrived, the time of your [?]. I spread my wings over you and covered your nakedness. I swore an oath to you and entered into a covenant with you, says Adonai the Lord, and you became mine.
And I washed you with water and cleansed you of your blood, and anointed you with oil.
And I clothed you in embroidered garments and put blue shoes on you. I wrapped fine linen around your waist and covered you with silk.
And I adorned you with ornaments, and put bracelets on your hands and a necklace around your neck.
I put earrings and pendants in your ears and a crown of glory on your head.

You adorned yourself with gold and silver ornaments, and your clothing was fine linen, gold-woven cloth, and embroidered cloth. You ate fine flour, oil, and honey. You became very, very beautiful and were pampered with royal luxuries.
And the fame of your beauty spread among all the nations, for your beauty was perfect through the splendor I had placed upon you, says the Lord Adonai.
You became proud of your beauty and prostituted yourself with your lovers. You offered your prostitution to every passerby, for whom there had been nothing like it.
You took some of your clothes and made patchwork idols for yourself, and you prostituted yourself with them. Do not go in there, for they did not exist and will not exist.
And you took your glorious ornaments, made from my gold and silver that I had given you, and made yourself male images and prostituted yourself with them.
You took your beautiful clothes and covered them, and you placed my oil and my incense before them.
And my bread, which I gave you—the fine flour, oil, and honey with which I fed you—you placed before them as a sweet fragrance. And this happened afterward, says Adonai the Lord.
You took your sons and daughters, whom you bore to me, and sacrificed them to those idols for destruction. Did you consider your prostitution a small thing?
You slaughtered my children and made them objects of destruction for those idols.

And this was more appalling than all your prostitution and abominations. You did not remember the days of your childhood, when you were naked, exposed, and wallowing in your blood, from which you were brought to life.
And after all your evil deeds—woe, woe to you, says Adonai the Lord—
you built yourself a house of prostitution and made yourself altars in all your public squares.
At the head of every road you built your places of prostitution. You spoiled the beauty of your face, spread yourself open to every passerby on the road, and multiplied your acts of prostitution.
You prostituted yourself with the Egyptians, your neighbors with large sexual organs, and multiplied your acts of prostitution to provoke me to anger.
Now I will stretch out my hand against you and take away your rights. I will deliver you into the hands of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who turned you aside from your way.
You acted wickedly and prostituted yourself with the Assyrians, yet even then you were not satisfied. You multiplied your acts of prostitution, yet even then you were not satisfied.
You multiplied your alliances with the land of Canaan and with all the Chaldeans, yet even then you were not satisfied.
What shall I do with your daughters, says Adonai the Lord, after you have done all these deeds of a prostitute? For you prostituted yourself repeatedly with your daughters.
You built places of prostitution at the head of every road and erected pillars in every public square. You were not like a prostitute who collects payment.
For every prostitute like you, who commits adultery with her own husband, takes no riches from her husband and pays her lovers.
All prostitutes receive payment for themselves, but you paid your lovers and sent for them to come to you from every direction for your prostitution.
In your prostitution you were the opposite of all other women, and no one sought you out for prostitution. They receive payment from men, but you paid your lovers, and so you were the opposite.
Therefore, prostitute, hear the words of the Lord.

Thus says Adonai the Lord: Because you poured out your copper, and the shame of your prostitution is to be exposed before your lovers, and because of all the schemes of your lawless deeds and the blood of your children whom you gave to them,

therefore, look, I will gather against you all your lovers with whom you had intercourse. I will raise up against you everyone you loved and everyone you hated. I will gather them and surround you with them, and I will expose your evil deeds before them, and they will see all your disgrace.
I will exact vengeance from you for adultery and bloodshed. I will leave you in your blood, and I will leave you in the blood of wrath and jealousy.
I will hand you over to them, and they will destroy your brothels and tear down your monuments. They will strip off your clothes, take away the crowns you boast of, and leave you naked and disgraced.
They will bring a mob against you, stone you with rocks, and cut you down with their swords.
They will burn your houses with fire and exact vengeance on you before many women. I will turn you away from your prostitution, and you will no longer pay them.
I will pour out my fury on you, and my jealousy will depart from you. I will be at rest and no longer troubled.

Because you did not remember the days of your youth, but distressed me with all these things, look, I have brought your own ways down on your head, says the Lord Adonai. And so you committed acts of impiety in addition to all your lawless deeds.
All this is what they murmured about you in proverbs, saying, ‘Like mother, like daughter.’

You are indeed the daughter of your mother, who rejected her husband and her children, and the sister of your sisters, who rejected their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite, and your father an Amorite.
Your older sister is Samaria, with her daughters, who lives to your left; and your younger sister, who lives to your right, is Sodom, with her daughters.
Yet you did not walk in their ways or act according to their lawless deeds, for you were found a little worse than they were in all your ways.
As I live, says the Lord Adonai, your sister Sodom and her daughters did not do anything worse than what you and your daughters have done.

But this was the lawlessness of your sister Sodom: arrogance amid an abundance of bread and a lavish supply of wine. She and her daughters lived indulgently; she and her daughters abounded in these things, but they did not extend a hand to the poor and needy.
They were arrogant and committed lawless deeds before me. When I saw this, I removed them.
Even Samaria did not commit half your sins. You multiplied your lawless deeds beyond theirs, and through all the lawless deeds you committed, you made your sisters appear righteous.

Now accept your punishment, you who corrupted your sisters through the lawless deeds you committed, worse than theirs. You made them appear far more righteous than yourself. Now be ashamed and bear your disgrace for making your sisters appear more righteous than yourself.
I will restore their fortunes—the fortunes of Sodom and her daughters. I will restore the fortunes of Samaria and her daughters, and I will restore your fortunes among them.
So that you may receive your punishment and be disgraced for everything you did to provoke me to anger.

Your sister Sodom and her daughters will be restored again as they were in the beginning. Samaria and her daughters will be restored again as they were in the beginning. You and your daughters will likewise be restored as you were in the beginning.
Was your sister Sodom not spoken of in your mouth in the days of your pride,
before your evils were revealed, as you have now become a reproach to the daughters of the Syrians and to all those around her, the daughters of the Philistines who surround you?
Now bear your acts of impiety and your lawless deeds, says the Lord.
For thus says the Lord Adonai: I will deal with you as you have acted, as you dishonored all that by transgressing my covenant.
I will remember my covenant that was with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish an everlasting covenant for myself.
You will remember your ways and be disgraced when you call to mind your sisters, the older ones together with the younger ones. I will give them to you as a test, and not as covenant partners.
And I will establish my covenant with you, and you will know that I am the Lord.
So that you may remember and be ashamed, and no longer be able to open your mouth because of your disgrace, when I forgive all the deeds you have done, says the Lord Adonai.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, tell a story and speak a parable to the house of Israel.
And you shall say: Thus says the Lord Adonai: A great eagle, with great wings, a wide wingspan, and abundant talons, resolved to enter Lebanon and took the choicest of the cedars.
And he took out the young shoot, carried it to the land of the Canaanites, and planted it in the walled city.
And he took some of the seed of the land and sowed it across the plain, a small sapling. He arranged for it to become conspicuous amid abundant water.
And it sprouted and became a weak vine, small in appearance, with its shoots appearing on it and its roots beneath it. And it became a great vine, produced clusters there, and sent out its tendrils.

And another great eagle appeared, with great wings and many talons. And behold, this vine was wrapped around it, its roots were in it, and its shoots were beneath it. And it sent out to have itself watered, together with the growth of its planting.
In the beautiful plain, with abundant water, it would thrive, sending out branches, bearing fruit, and becoming a great vine.

Therefore say: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Will it prosper? Will not its tender roots and its fruit rot, and all its branches wither? It will not take a mighty arm or many people to seize it and pull it up by its roots.
And now, will it thrive? It will not prosper. Will it not dry up, together with its growth and its branches, when the scorching wind approaches?
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, say to the house of Israel, the rebellious house: Do you not know what this saying means? When the king of Babylon comes to Jerusalem, he will take its king and its princes and carry them with him to Babylon.
And he will take someone from the royal offspring, make a covenant with him, bind him by curses, and take away the princes of the land,
so that it may be an utterly weak kingdom, never exalting itself, but keeping his covenant and remaining in it.

And he will rebel against him by sending messengers to Egypt to give him horses and many troops. Will he prosper? Will he survive? Will one who does such contrary things and breaks the covenant survive?
As I live, says Adonai the Lord, he who despised my curses and broke my covenant with him will surely die in the place where the king made him king, in the midst of Babylon.
And Pharaoh will not wage war alongside him with great strength or a large army. He will build siege ramps and platforms for shooting to destroy many lives.
For he despised the oath and broke the covenant. Look, I delivered him into his hands and did all this to him. Will he survive?
Therefore say: Thus says Adonai the Lord: As I live, says Adonai the Lord, I will surely repay him on his own head for my covenant that he broke and my oath that he despised.
And I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my trap. I will bring him to Babylon, and there I will judge him for the wrong he committed against me.
And in all his escapes, in all his battles, they will fall by the sword. I will scatter his survivors to every wind, and you will know that I, the Lord, have spoken.

Therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: I myself will take from the choicest of the choice, lofty cedars and give it. From the top of its shoots, from their hearts, I will pluck it and plant it on a high mountain.

And I will hang it from the lofty mountain of Israel; I will plant it, and it will send out branches and bear fruit and become a great cedar. All wild animals will rest beneath it, and all flying birds will dwell under its shade, and its tendrils will become firmly established on it.

And all the trees of the field will know that I am the Lord, who brings the tall tree low and raises the low tree high, dries up the green tree and makes the withered tree green. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will do it.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, what is this proverb you have among the children of Israel, which says: The fathers ate sour grapes, and the children's teeth were set on edge?
As I live, says Adonai the Lord, this proverb will no longer be spoken among Israel.
For all souls are mine. The father's soul and the son's soul are equally mine. The soul that sins will itself die.
But if a man is righteous and practices justice and righteousness,

does not eat what has been sacrificed on the mountains, does not turn his eyes toward the idols of the house of Israel, does not defile his neighbor's wife, and does not approach his own wife during her menstrual period,
does not oppress anyone, returns the debtor's pledge, does not commit robbery, gives his bread to the hungry, and clothes the naked,
He does not lend his silver at interest or demand repayment with interest. He turns his hands away from wrongdoing and judges fairly between a man and his neighbor.
He walks according to my commands, keeps my ordinances, and carries them out. He is righteous; he will surely live, says the Lord GOD.
But if he fathers a wayward son who sheds blood and commits sins,
who does not walk in the ways of his righteous father, but eats sacrificial food on the mountains and defiles his neighbor’s wife,
oppresses the poor and needy, commits robbery, does not return a pledge, turns his eyes toward the worship of gods, and commits lawlessness,
lends his silver at interest and demands usury and interest—he shall not live. Since he has committed all these lawless deeds, he shall surely die, and his blood shall be upon himself.
But if he fathers a son who sees all the sins his father committed, fears, and does not do the same things,
does not eat sacrificial food on the mountains, does not turn his eyes toward the idols of the house of Israel, and does not defile his neighbor’s wife,
does not oppress anyone, does not take a pledge, does not commit robbery, gives his bread to the hungry, and clothes the naked,
turns his hands away from wrongdoing, takes neither usury nor interest, does what is righteous, and walks according to my commands—he shall not die for his father’s wrongdoing, but shall surely live.
But his father, if he cruelly oppresses and robs his brother and commits acts of hostility among my people, shall die for his own wrongdoing.

And you say, ‘Why has the father’s wrongdoing not fallen upon the son?’ Because the son has shown mercy and done what is righteous, has kept all my laws, and has carried them out, he shall surely live.

The person who sins shall die. The son shall not bear his father’s sins, nor shall the father bear his son’s wrongdoing. The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon himself, and the lawlessness of the lawless shall be upon himself.
But if the lawless person turns away from all the lawless deeds he has committed, keeps all my commandments, and practices righteousness and mercy, he shall surely live and shall not die.
Let none of the offenses he committed or the injustices he perpetrated be remembered. Rather, he will live through the righteousness he practiced.
Do I really desire the sinner’s death, says the Lord GOD, rather than his turning from his evil way and living?

But when the righteous person turns away from his righteousness and commits wrongdoing according to all the lawless deeds the lawless person commits, none of the righteous deeds he has done shall be remembered. He shall die for the transgressions into which he fell and the sins he committed.
And you say, ‘The Lord’s way is not fair.’ Now listen, house of Israel: Is my way not fair? Is it not your ways that are unfair?
When the righteous person turns away from his righteousness and commits wrongdoing, he shall die for the lawlessness he has committed.
And when the lawless person turns away from the lawlessness he has committed and practices justice and righteousness, he saves his own life.
Because he saw and turned away from all the ungodly deeds he had committed, he shall surely live and shall not die.
And the house of Israel says, ‘The Lord’s way is not right.’ Is my way not right, house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are wrong?
Therefore I will judge each of you according to his own way, house of Israel, says the Lord GOD. Repent and turn away from all your ungodly deeds, and wrongdoing will not bring punishment upon you.

Cast away from yourselves all the wicked deeds by which you have acted wickedly against me. Make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit, and carry out all my commandments. Why should you die, house of Israel? says the Lord.
For I do not desire the death of the sinner, says Adonai, the Lord, but that he should turn from his evil ways and preserve his life. Now come, turn back, and live.
A lament over the ruler of Israel
And you, son of man, take up a lament over the ruler of Israel,
and say: Why did your mother become a lion cub among lions? Among lions she multiplied her cubs.
One of her cubs grew up and became a lion. He learned to seize prey and became a devourer of people.
The nations heard about him. They caught him in a pit and brought him to the land of the Egyptians with a muzzle in his mouth.
She saw that she was separated from him and that her hope was lost. Then she made another of her cubs into a lion.
And he went about among lions and became a lion. He learned to seize prey and became a devourer of people.
He hunted boldly, destroyed cities, and devastated the land and everything in it with the sound of his roar.
The nations rose against him from the surrounding countries and enclosed him with traps in a pit.
They put a muzzle in his mouth and brought him in a cage to the king of the Babylonians. They put him in prison so that his voice would no longer be heard on the mountains of Israel.
Your mother was like a vine and like a pomegranate blossom planted beside flowing waters. Its growth and its fruit came from abundant water.
It had a strong scepter over the nation of rulers. It grew tall among the thickets and saw its own greatness in the abundance of its branches.
It was broken in anger and thrown down to the ground. A scorching wind dried up its shoots. Vengeance was exacted from it, its strong scepter dried up, and fire consumed it.
And now they have planted it in the wilderness, in a land without water.
And fire came out from its choicest branches and consumed it, and there was no strong rod in it. A people serves as a parable of mourning, and it will become a lament.
To the elders of the house of Israel
In the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, some of the elders of the house of Israel came to inquire of the Lord and sat before me.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, speak to these elders of the house of Israel and say to them: Thus says the Lord Adonai: Have you come to inquire of me? As I live, I will give you no answer, says the Lord Adonai.
Shall I take vengeance on them, son of man? Testify to them about the sins of their fathers,

and say to them: Thus says the Lord God: From the day when I set my desire on the house of Israel and made myself known to the descendants of the house of Jacob, I made myself known to them in the land of the Egyptians. I pledged to them and said, I am the Lord your God.
On that day I pledged to them that I would bring them out of the land of the Egyptians into the land I had prepared for them, a land flowing with milk and honey, sweeter than every other land.
And I said to them: Let each of you cast away the abominations before your eyes, and do not defile yourselves with the practices of the Egyptians. I am the Lord your God.

But they rebelled against me and refused to listen to me. None of them cast away the abominations before their eyes, and they did not abandon the practices of the Egyptians. So I said that I would pour out my fury upon them and fully unleash my anger against them among the Egyptians.
But I acted so that my name would not be profaned at all before the nations among whom they lived, in whose sight I made myself known to them by bringing them out of the land of the Egyptians.
I brought them out of the land of the Egyptians and led them into the wilderness.
And I gave them my commands and showed them my ordinances, which a person shall carry out and live by them.

I gave them my Sabbaths to be a sign between me and them, so that they would know that I am the Lord who makes them holy. And I said to the house of Israel there in the wilderness: Walk according to my commands—but they did not walk according to them—and keep my laws and carry them out; if a person carries them out, he will live by them.

And the house of Israel provoked me in the wilderness. They did not walk according to my commands and rejected my ordinances, which, if a person carries them out, he will live by them. They greatly profaned my Sabbaths, and I said I would pour out my wrath in the wilderness to destroy them.
And I acted so that my name would not be profaned at all before the nations from among whom I brought them out in their sight.
And I raised my hand over them in the wilderness, declaring that I would not bring them into the land I had given them, a land flowing with milk and honey, sweeter than every other land.
Because they rejected my judgments, did not walk according to my commands, profaned my Sabbaths, and followed the thoughts of their own hearts.
Yet my eye spared them from destruction, and I did not make a complete end of them in the wilderness.
And I said to them in the wilderness, “Do not follow the practices of your fathers, do not keep their judgments, and do not join in their ways or defile yourselves.
I am the Lord your God. Walk according to my commands, keep my judgments, and carry them out.
And keep my Sabbaths holy, and they shall be a sign between me and you, so that you may know that I am the Lord your God.”

Their children also provoked me. They did not walk according to my commands and did not take care to carry out my judgments, which a person shall live by if he carries them out. They profaned my Sabbaths, and I said that I would pour out my wrath upon them in the wilderness and exhaust my anger upon them.
But I turned my hand away from them and acted so that my name would not be profaned at all before the nations from among whom I brought them out in their sight.
And I raised my hand over them there in the wilderness, declaring that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them throughout the provinces.
Because they did not carry out my judgments, rejected my commands, and profaned my Sabbaths, and their eyes followed the thoughts of their fathers.
And I gave them commands that were not good and judgments by which they would not live.
And I defiled them through their offerings, when I passed through everyone who opens the womb, so that I might destroy them and they might know that I am the Lord.
Therefore speak to the house of Israel, son of man, and say to them, “Thus says the Lord GOD: To this extent your fathers provoked me by the transgressions they committed against me.

And I brought them into the land that I had raised my hand to give them. There they saw every high hill and every leafy tree, and there they sacrificed to their gods, set out their sacrificial offerings, burned their fragrant incense, and dedicated their gifts.
And I said to them, ‘What is this Abbana that you enter?’ And they called its name Abbana, down to this very day.
Therefore say to the house of Israel, ‘Thus says the Lord God: If you defile yourselves with the lawlessness of your fathers and prostitute yourselves by following their abominations,

and with the produce of your offerings and the gifts of your children, and by setting apart your children to lead them through the flame, you defile yourselves in all your schemes down to this very day, shall I give you an answer, house of Israel? As I live, says the Lord GOD, I will not give you an answer.
And what comes into your minds shall not happen, when you say, “Let us be like the heathen and like the nations of the earth, serving wood and stones.”
Therefore, as I live, says the Lord GOD, I will surely reign over you with a mighty hand, an uplifted arm, and wrath poured out.
And I will bring you out from the nations and gather you from the lands where you have been scattered, with a mighty hand, an uplifted arm, and wrath poured out.
And I will bring you into the wilderness of the nations, and there I will enter into judgment with you face to face.
Just as I passed judgment on your fathers there in the wilderness, when I brought them out of the land of the Egyptians, so I will judge you, says the Lord, the Lord God.
And I will make you pass under my rod and bring you under the reckoning of my covenant.
And I will separate the ungodly and the rebels from among you, for I will bring them out of their dwelling place, but they will not enter the land of Israel. And you will know that I am the Lord God.

And you, house of Israel, thus says the Lord, the Lord God: First, let each of you put away his own practices. Then, if you listen to me, you will no longer defile my holy name with your sacrifices and your practices.

For on my holy mountain, on the high mountain of Israel, says the Lord, the Lord, there the entire house of Israel will serve me. There I will accept you, and there I will attend to your offerings and the firstfruits of all your holy gifts.
I will accept you as a pleasing fragrance when I bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the countries where you were scattered. And through you I will show myself holy before the peoples.
And you will know that I am the Lord when I bring you into the land of Israel, into the land that I raised my hand and swore to give to your fathers.
There you will remember your ways and your practices by which you defiled yourselves, and you will beat your faces over all the injustices you committed.
And you will know that I am the Lord when I do this to you so that my name will not be defiled by your evil ways and your corrupt practices, says Adonai, the Lord.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, set your face toward Teman, look toward Dagov, and prophesy against the forest of the ruler of the Negeb.

And say to the forest of the Negeb: Hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord, the Lord God: See, I will kindle a fire in you, and it will consume every green tree and every dry tree in you. The blazing flame will not be extinguished, and every face from east to north will be burned by it.
And all flesh will know that I, the Lord, kindled it, and it will not be extinguished.
And I said: Far be it, Lord, Lord! They say to me, ‘Is not what you are saying a parable?’
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Therefore prophesy, son of man, and set your face against Jerusalem. Look toward their sanctuaries and prophesy against the land of Israel.
And say to the land of Israel: Thus says the Lord, the Lord God: See, I am against you. I will draw my sword from its sheath and destroy the unjust and the lawless from your midst.
Because I will destroy the unjust and the lawless from you, my sword will therefore come out of its sheath against all flesh, from east to north.
And all flesh will know that I, the Lord, have drawn my sword from its sheath, and it will no longer return.
And you, son of man, groan with your waist broken, and groan in pain before them.

And if they say to you, ‘Why are you groaning?’ say: ‘Because I have heard bad news, and it is coming. Every heart will break, every hand will go limp, all flesh and every spirit will dry up, and all loins will be fouled with moisture. See, it is coming, and it will happen,’ says the Lord, the Lord God.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says Adonai, the Lord. And say: Sword, sword, sharpen yourself and rage!
Sharpen yourself to carry out a slaughter. Be polished; prepare for destruction. Slaughter! Despise, my son; cut away every tree.
And he gave it to be held ready in his hand. The sword has been sharpened; it is ready to be put into the hand of the slaughterer.

Raise your voice, lift up a cry, son of man, for it has come upon my people and upon the rulers of Israel. They will become exiles, because the sword has come upon my people. Therefore clap your hands, for it has been justified.
And what? Will the nation survive? It will not, says the Lord, the Lord.
And you, son of man, prophesy. Clap your hands; double the sword, for the third sword is the sword of the wounded. The sword of the wounded has grown fierce, and it will terrify them.

So that their hearts may break and the weakened may multiply at all their gates, for they have been handed over to slaughter by the sword. It has been made beautiful by its gleam and made fit for slaughter.
Turn, range about, sharpen yourself to the right and to the left, wherever your face is roused.
And there I will clap my hands and dance and let my voice ring out. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:

And you, son of man, prepare for yourself two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon to enter, so that both routes come out of one land. Set up a pointing hand at the head of the road to the city; station yourself at the beginning of the road.
And you, prepare and arrange a road for the sword to enter through Rabbah of the Ammonites, against Judea and against Jerusalem within it.
For the king of Babylon will come and stand on the old road, at the head of the two roads, to practice divination, cast rods, inquire of idols, and divine by examining a liver.

On his right the omens came out for Jerusalem: to erect a siege ramp, shout with his mouth wide open, raise his voice in a battle cry, set barricades against its gates, heap up earth, and build towers for archers.
And to them it will seem as though someone were practicing divination before them and counting out sevens for them; but he himself will bring their injustices to remembrance.

Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have brought your injustices to remembrance by exposing your ungodliness, so that your sins appear in all your ungodly acts and in your conduct, because you yourselves have brought them to remembrance, you will perish in them.
And you, defiled and lawless ruler of Israel, whose day of the end has come in the time of injustice,
thus says the Lord God: Remove your turban and take off your crown, for this will not end in this way. You have brought down the exalted and raised up the lowly.
Now I will lay injustice upon injustices on him, and this will not remain so until the one to whom it rightfully belongs comes, and I will give it into his hands.
And you, son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord God to the Ammonites and concerning their insults. Say: A sword, a sword drawn for slaughter, unsheathed for destruction!

Awake, so that you may flash! Through a worthless vision and the divining of false omens, it is delivered to you against the necks of the wounded lawless people, whose day of the end has arrived in the time of injustice.
Turn back; do not rest here. In the place where you were born, back in your own land, I will judge you.
And I will pour out my anger upon you; with the fire of my wrath I will blow upon you, and I will deliver you into the hands of barbarous men who bring about destruction.
And you will become food for the fire, and your blood will be in the midst of your land, and no remembrance of you will be found, for I, the Lord, have spoken.
To the Israelites
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
And you, son of man, if you judge, judge the city of bloodshed and expose all its lawless deeds.
And say: Thus says the Lord God: O city that sheds blood within itself, so that its time may come, and devises a plan concerning itself, to defile itself with their blood!
