You were stained by the [?] you shed, and you were defiled by the plans you devised. You have brought your days near and brought on the time of your years. Therefore I have made you an object of reproach to the nations and of mockery to all lands.
Those who were near you and those far from you will mock you and say, “Your name has been disgraced, because you have multiplied your lawless deeds.”
Look, the leaders of the house of Israel, each with the relatives of his own clan, joined together within you to shed blood.
They dishonored father and mother within you, and acted unjustly toward the newcomer and the foreign resident within you. They oppressed the orphan and the widow within you.
They despised my holy things and profaned my Sabbaths within you.
Robbers were among you to shed blood within you, and they offered sacrifices on the mountains within you and committed unclean acts in your midst.
They exposed their fathers’ nakedness within you, and in impurity they violated menstruating women within you.
And each defiled his neighbor’s wife, and each defiled his daughter-in-law in ungodliness, and each violated his sister, his father’s daughter, within you.

They take bribes within you to shed blood; they take usury and interest within you. I will bring about and complete the end of your evils in keeping with your violence, because you have forgotten me, says the Lord God.
Look, I will clap my hands over the deeds you have done and over the bloodshed committed within you.
Will your heart endure, and will your hands be strong in the days when I deal with you? I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will act.
I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you among the provinces, and your uncleanness will diminish within you.
I will take possession of you in the sight of the nations, and you will know that I am the Lord.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, look: the house of Israel has become a mixed alloy to me, like copper, iron, tin, lead, and silver mixed together in a furnace.
Therefore say: Thus says the Lord God: Because you have all become one mixed mass, I will gather you into Jerusalem.
As someone gathers silver, copper, iron, and lead into a furnace to blow fire upon it and melt it, so I will gather you in my anger; I will collect you and melt you.
I will crush you with fire in my anger, and you will be melted within it.
As silver is melted in a furnace, so you will be melted within it, and you will know that I, the Lord, have poured out my wrath upon you.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, say to it: You are a land that is not watered and upon which no rain fell on the day of anger.
Its rulers within it roared like lions, seizing prey. They devour the lives of the poor by violence and take honors unjustly, and widows have multiplied within you.

Its priests dishonored my laws and profaned my holy things. They did not distinguish the holy from the profane or separate the unclean from the clean. They hid their eyes from my Sabbaths and profaned my Sabbaths among them.
Its rulers within it are like ravenous wolves, seizing prey, shedding blood, and destroying lives so that they may acquire great gain through greed.
Its prophets who plastered over them will fall. They saw empty visions, desired lies for them, and said, “Thus says Adonai, the Lord,” although the Lord had not spoken.
They oppressed the people of the land unjustly and seized plunder. They subjected the poor and needy to violence and did not deal justly with the foreigner.
I sought among them one man who would walk uprightly and stand confidently before me in the time of anger, so that I would not destroy it, but I found none.
I poured out my wrath upon them, to consume them with the fire of my anger. I brought their own ways down upon their heads, says the Lord God.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother.
They prostituted themselves in Egypt in their youth. There their breasts sagged; there they lost their virginity.
The name of the elder daughter was Oholah, and her sister was Oholibah. They became mine and bore sons and daughters. As for their names, Samaria was Oholah and Jerusalem was Oholibah.
Oholah prostituted herself, turning away from me, and cast her eyes after her lovers, the Assyrians who were near her,
clothed in blue and scarlet: rulers and military commanders, all of them chosen young men, fully armed, riding horses.
She extended her prostitution to them, to all the chosen sons of the Assyrians, and to everyone she pursued. She defiled herself with all her schemes.

She did not abandon her prostitution from the land of the Egyptians, for she had defiled herself with them from her youth. They deprived her of her virginity and poured out their prostitution upon her.
Therefore they handed her over to her lovers, into the hands of the sons of the Assyrians whom she pursued.
They exposed her disgrace, took her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword. She became a byword among women, and they took vengeance on her among her daughters.
Her sister Oholibah saw this and became even more shameless in her corruption than she was, and her prostitution exceeded her sister’s prostitution.
For she pursued the Assyrian men, rulers and commanders who were near her, dressed in purple garments, noblemen fully armed, riding horses, all of them choice young men.
And I saw that she had defiled herself; both followed the same path.
She increased her prostitution and saw men painted on walls, images of Chaldeans drawn with a brush in paint,
wearing various belts around their waists and dyed turbans on their heads. All of them were striking in many colors, resembling Babylonian men in the land of the Chaldeans, their native country.
She desired them when she looked at them with her eyes, and she sent messengers to them in the land of the Chaldeans.
The sons of Babylon came to her bed to lie with her, and they defiled her through their prostitution. She was defiled with them, and her soul became disgusted with them.
She revealed her prostitution and made her shame public. And my soul turned away from her, just as my soul had turned away from her sister.
You increased your prostitution, recalling the days of your youth, when you prostituted yourself in Egypt.
You turned your eyes toward the Chaldeans, whose genitals were like those of donkeys and horses.
I will punish the lawlessness of your youth, which you practiced in the land of the Egyptians, in your lodgings, where your breasts fell and your virginity was lost.
Therefore, Oholibah, thus says the Lord, the Lord: Look, I will stir up against you the lovers with whom your soul became disgusted, and I will bring them to surround you:
the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, Pekod, Shoa, and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them—choice young men, rulers, commanders, fully armed and renowned men, riding horses.

They will all come against you from the north, with chariots and wheels and a multitude of peoples, wearing helmets and carrying shields. They will set a guard around you. I will place judgment before them, and they will exact vengeance from you according to their judgments.

I will direct my jealousy against you, and they will deal with you according to my anger and fury. They will cut off your nose and ears and slaughter those who remain of you with the sword. They will take your sons and daughters and destroy those who remain of you with fire.
They will strip your clothes from you and take the ornaments in which you take pride.
I will put an end to your ungodliness and to your prostitution in the land of the Egyptians. You will not lift your eyes toward it or remember Egypt anymore.
Therefore, thus says the Lord, the Lord: Look, I will deliver you into the hands of those who hate you, with whom your soul became disgusted.

They will deal with you in hatred and take all the fruits of your labor and toil. You will be naked and disgraced, and the shame of your prostitution, your ungodliness, and your prostitution will be exposed.
They did these things to you because you prostituted yourself by pursuing the nations, defiling yourself with their practices.
You followed your sister’s ways, and I will put her cup into your hand.
Thus says the Lord, the Lord: You will drink your sister’s cup, deep and wide, and you will become an object of laughter and mockery, drinking deeply until you are completely drunk.
And you will be filled with despair from the cup of ruin, the cup of your sister Samaria.
You will drink it and drain it, tear out your hair, and rip your breasts. I will remove your festivals and your new moons from you, for I have spoken, says Adonai the Lord.
Therefore the Lord God says this: Because you forgot me and cast me behind your back, you too must bear your ungodliness and your prostitution.
And the Lord said to me: Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah and tell them of their lawless deeds?
For they committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. In their schemes they committed adultery, and they passed through the flames their children whom they had borne to me.
They even did this to me: they defiled my holy places on that same day and violated my Sabbaths.
When they sacrificed their children to their idols, they entered my holy places on that same day and defiled them. This is what they did within my house.
For men coming from far away, to whom they sent messengers, as soon as they arrived you went into the baths, painted yourself with eye paint and rouge, and adorned yourself with ornaments.
You sat on adorned couches and placed a prepared table before you. You took my incense and the oils and rejoiced with them.

They played music to the sound of skilled performers. Along with those men, there was also a crowd of drunken men who had come from the wilderness. You put bracelets on their hands and crowns of glory on their heads.
And I said: Let her not commit adultery with them by engaging in prostitution. But she prostituted herself.
They went in to her as men go in to a prostitute. In the same way they went in to Oholah and Oholibah to commit lawless deeds.
They were righteous men, and they will exact vengeance from them—the vengeance due to adulteresses and the vengeance due for bloodshed—for they were adulteresses, and blood was on their hands.
For thus says the Lord God: “Bring an army against them, and cast turmoil and plunder upon them.”
Stone them with the troops’ stones and wound them with their swords. Their sons and daughters will be slaughtered, and their houses will be burned.
I will remove ungodliness from the land, and all women will be warned and will no longer act according to their ungodliness.
Your ungodliness will be laid upon you, and you will receive what the sins of your schemes deserve. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
And the word of the Lord came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, saying:
Son of man, record for yourself the date of the day on which the king of Babylon came against Jerusalem.
From that day, tell this parable to the rebellious house and say to them: The Lord God says this: Set the pot in place, set it in place, and pour water into it.
Put the portions into it, every fine piece of meat—the thigh and the rib separated from the bones—
taken from the choicest of the choice animals. Burn the bones beneath the pot. It boiled and bubbled; it boiled vigorously, and the bones were cooked among them.
Therefore the Lord God says this: O city of bloodshed, a pot full of rust whose rust has not been cleared away! He took its contents out piece by piece, and no lot fell upon it.
For its blood is within it. I placed it on a bare rock and did not pour it onto the ground to cover it with earth.
So that my fury might rise in vengeance to exact retribution, I placed its blood on the bare rock, so that it would not be covered.
Therefore the Lord God says this: Woe to the city of bloodshed! I too will heap up the wood
and multiply the firebrands and kindle the fire, so that the meat melts away, the broth diminishes, and the bones crumble.
Let it stand on its coals. It blazed up so that it might burn and grow hot, its copper might melt along with the impurity inside it, and its rust might disappear.
And let its rust diminish, but let its abundant rust not come out of it, and let its rust be put to shame by the uncleanness of the broth.
Because you defiled yourself and will not be cleansed of your uncleanness—and what will happen if it is still not cleansed until I have fully poured out my wrath upon it?

I, the Lord, have spoken, and it will come, and I will act. I will not shrink back, nor will I have pity, nor will I relent. Instead, I will judge you according to your ways and your conduct, says the Lord God. Therefore I will judge you according to your bloodshed, and according to your plans I will judge you, you unclean slanderer, who have multiplied your provocations.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, look, I am taking away from you the delight of your eyes through war. You shall not mourn or weep, and no tears shall flow from you.
For groaning is in the midst of blood and mourning. Your hair shall not be braided, and your shoes shall remain on your feet. Do not take comfort from their lips, and do not eat the bread of men.
And I spoke to the people in the morning, as the Lord had commanded me, and my wife died in the evening. In the morning I did as I had been commanded.
The people said to me, “Will you not tell us what these things you are doing mean?”
And I say to them: The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Look, I will defile my sanctuary, the pride of your strength, the delight of your eyes, and what your souls cherish. Your sons and your daughters whom you have left behind shall fall by the sword.
And you shall do just as I have done. Do not take comfort from their mouths, and you shall not eat the bread of men.
Your hair shall remain on your heads and your shoes on your feet. You shall not mourn or weep, but you shall waste away in your iniquities, and no one shall comfort his brother.
And Ezekiel shall be a sign to you. You shall do everything that he has done. When this happens, you shall know that I am the Lord God.
And you, son of man, surely on that day, when I take away from them their strength, the pride of their glory, the delight of their eyes, and the pride of their souls—their sons and their daughters—
on that day a survivor shall come to you to bring news to your ears.
On that day your mouth shall be opened to the survivor. You shall speak and shall no longer be mute. You shall be a sign to them, and they shall know that I am the Lord.
Concerning the Ammonites
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, set your face against the Ammonites and prophesy against them.

And you shall say to the Ammonites: Hear the words of the Lord God. Thus says the Lord God: Because you trampled upon my holy places when they were defiled, and upon the land of Israel when it was laid waste, and upon the house of Judah when it went into captivity,

therefore, look, I am handing you over to the people of the East as a possession. They shall settle in you with their [?] and pitch their tents in you. They shall eat your fruit and drink your richness.
And I will make the city of the Ammonites a pasture for camels, and the Ammonites a pasture for flocks, and you shall know that I am the Lord.
For thus says the Lord God: Because you clapped your hands and stamped your feet and rejoiced in your soul over the land of Israel,

therefore, look, I will stretch out my hand against you and give you over to plunder among the nations. I will wipe you out from among the peoples and utterly destroy you from the lands, and you shall know that I am the Lord. Concerning Moab
Thus says the Lord God: Because Moab and Seir said, ‘Look, the house of Israel and Judah is just like all the nations,’
Therefore, look, I will tear open Moab’s flank, stripping away its lofty cities, the choicest land, the house of Beth and Asimoth, above the city’s spring by the seashore.
The sons of Kedem will come against the Ammonites, and I gave it to him as an inheritance, so that the Ammonites may no longer be remembered among the nations.
And I will take vengeance on Moab, and they will know that I am the Lord.
Against Edom. Thus says the Lord God: Because Edom took vengeance on the house of Judah, and they bore a grudge and exacted vengeance,

therefore thus says the Lord God: I will stretch out my hand against Edom and destroy both people and animals from it. I will make it a wilderness, and those fleeing from Teman will fall by the sword.
And I will take vengeance on Edom through my people Israel. They will deal with Edom according to my anger and fury, and they will know my vengeance, says the Lord God.
Against the Philistines. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because the foreigners bore a grudge and stirred up vengeance with malice in their hearts, trampling others down to destroy them forever,
therefore thus says the Lord God: Look, I will stretch out my hand against those foreigners, destroy those Cretans, and wipe out the survivors along those seacoasts.
And I will exact great vengeance from them with rebuke and anger. They will know that I am the Lord God when I exact my vengeance from them.
Against Tyre.
And in the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, because Tyre mocked Jerusalem and said, ‘Aha, aha! She is broken and destroyed! The nations will turn to me, because she who was full has been laid waste,’
therefore thus says the Lord God: Look, I am against you, Tyre, and I will bring many nations against you, as the sea rises with its waves.
They will demolish Tyre’s walls and bring down its towers. I will sweep its soil away from it and make it a bare rock.
There will be places for spreading nets in the midst of the sea, for I have spoken, says the Lord God. And it will become plunder for the nations.
And its daughters in the open country will be killed by the sword, and they will know that I am the Lord.

For thus says the Lord God: Look, I will bring against you, Tyre, Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians, from the north. He is king of kings, coming with chariots and horses, with troops upon troops of cavalry from very many nations.
He will slaughter your daughters in the open country with the sword. He will post a guard all around you, dig a trench, raise a siege ramp, and establish a fortified line of weapons.
He will set up his spears against you and demolish your wall and towers with his sword.

Because of the multitude of his horsemen, their dust will cover you. At the sound of the horsemen and the wheels of their chariots, your walls will shake when he enters your gates, as someone enters a city from the open country.
With their horses’ hooves they will trample your streets. He will slaughter your people with the sword and bring the stronghold of your power down to the ground.
He will plunder your resources and loot your possessions. He will demolish your walls and pull down your splendid palaces, and he will cast the stones, timber, and soil into the sea.
He will put an end to your many artisans, and the sound of songs will no longer be heard in you.
I will make you a bare rock, and you will become a place for spreading nets. You will never be rebuilt, for I have spoken, says the Lord God.
For thus says the Lord God to Tyre: Will not your islands shake at the sound of your downfall, at the groaning of your wounded, when the sword is drawn in your midst?

All the princes of the nations of your sea will come down from their thrones, remove their crowns from their heads, and strip off their varied garments. They will be overcome with distress, fall to the ground, and be terrified at their own destruction, and they will sigh over you.

They will raise a lament over you and say, “How you have perished and been torn apart in the midst of the sea, you magnificent city! You and your inhabitants were mighty in the midst of the sea, and you terrified all your inhabitants.”
The islands will be afraid on the day of your downfall, and the islands of your sea will be shaken when you are stripped bare.
For thus says the Lord, the Lord: “When I make you a ruined city, like cities that have never been inhabited, when I bring the depths up over you and many waters cover you,

“I will bring you down to those who descend into the pit, to the people of ancient times. I will make you dwell in the depths of the earth, like the ancient ruins, with those who descended long ago into the pit, so that you will no longer be inhabited or stand in the land of the living.”
I will hand you over to destruction, and you will be no more. You will be sought, but you will never be found.”
Lamentations over Tyre
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, raise a lament over Tyre.
You shall say to Tyre, who dwells at the entrances to the sea and trades with peoples from many islands: “Thus says the Lord God to Tyre:
You used to say, “I adorned myself with the splendor of my beauty.” In the heart of the sea, your sons of Beelim adorned you.
Cedars from Mount Senir were made into braces and planks for you. Cypresses were taken from Lebanon to make firwood masts for you.
From Bashan they made the rudders of your ships, and they built your shrines of ivory, densely wooded palaces from the islands of the Kittim.
Fine linen with embroidery from Egypt was made into your sailcloth, to clothe you in splendor. Purple and blue cloth from the islands of [?] became the adornment of your coverings.
Your princes were inhabitants of Sidon, and men of Arvad were your sailors. Your wise men, Tyre, who were within you, were your ship captains.
The elders, scribes, and its wise men who were within you strengthened your counsels. All the ships of the sea and their sailors were at your service to travel to the farthest west.
The Lydians and Libyans supported your strength, chosen warriors who hung their shields and helmets within you, and they brought you glory.
The sons of the men of Arvad, with their forces, stood all around your walls and guarded your towers. They hung their quivers all around your walls, and they themselves perfected your beauty.
The Carthaginians were your merchants because of the abundance of all your wealth. They supplied silver, gold, bronze, iron, tin, and lead to your markets.
The Greeks and all those around them were your slave traders, and they supplied bronze vessels to your markets.
From the house of Togarmah they filled your markets with horses, horsemen, and mules.
The sons of the Rhodians were your merchants. From the islands they increased your trade with ivory tusks, and you gave people as payment to the travelers.
Your trade multiplied because of your abundance. Liquid myrrh from Aphek, multicolored cords from Tarshish, and Ramoth and Karkod filled your markets.
Judea and the sons of Israel were your merchants. With wheat, incense, cassia, the choicest honey, oil, and resin, they filled your markets with abundant goods.
Damascus was your trading partner because of your abundance and your great wealth, with wine from Helbon and wool from Miletus.
Dan and Javan from Meozena brought you wine for your markets; from Asela came worked iron and covered wheels for your markets.
The Dedanites were your merchants. They brought choice chariots together with mules.
The Arabs and all the princes of Kedar were merchants under your authority. They traded camels, rams, and ewes with you.
Sheba and Raamah were also your merchants. They supplied fragrant oils, precious stones, and gold to your markets.
Harran, Canaan, and Dedan were your merchants; Sheba, Assyria, and Chalman were your merchants.
They brought you merchandise from Machlim and Galim: purple, scarlet, blue, and multicolored woven bands, and choice treasures enclosed and bound with ropes,
in cypress ships, with which your trade was carried on. With your ships, the abundance of your merchandise, and the multitude of your mixed company, you became full and exceedingly heavy.
Your pilots steered you into the heart of the sea, into great waters. A south wind shattered you in the heart of the sea.

Your strength, your earnings, your mixed company, your pilots, your shipmasters, your counselors, the mixed company among your mixed company, all your fighting men within you, and the whole assembly in your midst will fall into the heart of the sea on the day of your destruction.
At the sound of your voice, your pilots will tremble with fear.
All your pilots and your sailors will come down from their ships; the ships’ lookouts will stand on the seashore.
They will cry out over you, raise their voices, and lament bitterly. They will put earth on their heads and roll in ashes.
They will shave their heads bald and dress in sackcloth. They will weep over you with embittered hearts, with bitter mourning.
Their sons will take up a lament over you; they will take it up and lament: “Who was like Tyre, which has fallen silent and ceased in the midst of the sea?
With all the earnings you obtained from that sea, you satisfied the nations. With your abundance and your multitude of merchandise, you made all the kings of the earth great.
Now you have been shattered in the sea, in the depths of the waters. Your merchandise and your whole assembly within you have fallen, along with all your pilots.
All the inhabitants of the islands grieved over you, and their kings trembled greatly and shed tears down their faces over you.
The merchants of the nations hissed at you. You have been given over to destruction and will never exist again,” says the Lord God.
Concerning the ruler of Tyre
The word of the Lord came to me and said:

And you, son of man, say to the ruler of Tyre: Thus says the Lord God: Because your heart grew proud and you said, “I am God, and I have lived in God’s dwelling in the heart of the sea,” you are a man and not God, yet you have made your heart like the heart of God.
Are you wiser than Daniel, or have wise men instructed you with their understanding?
Was it by your wisdom or your counsel that you gained wealth for yourself and acquired gold and silver in your treasuries?
Or did you increase your wealth through your great wisdom and trade, and did your heart become exalted because of your wealth?
Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have made your heart like the heart of God,

therefore, behold, I will bring foreigners against you, evildoers from the nations. They will draw their swords against you and against the beauty of your wisdom, and they will give your beauty over to destruction.
They will bring you down, and you will die the death of the wounded in the heart of the sea.
Will you still say, “I am God,” before your attackers? But you are a man and not God.
And among your many wounded, you will die the death of the uncircumcised at the hands of foreigners, for I have spoken, says Adonai the Lord.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, take up a lament over the ruler of Tyre and say to him: Thus says the Lord God: You are the seal of likeness, full of wisdom and a crown of beauty.

You were amid the delights of the paradise of God, and you fastened every precious stone upon yourself: sardius, topaz, emerald, carbuncle, sapphire, jasper, silver and gold, jacinth, agate, amethyst, chrysolite, beryl, and onyx. You filled your treasuries and your storehouses within you with gold from the day you were established and made ready.
I placed you with the anointed cherub. You were on the holy mountain of God, among the fiery rocks.
“You were blameless throughout your days, from the day you were established until injustices were found in you.”

Through the abundance of your trade, you filled your storehouses with wrongdoing. You sinned and were wounded. The cherub with flowing hair brought you down from the mountain of God, from among the fiery rocks.
Your heart became proud because of your beauty, and your wisdom was corrupted along with your beauty. Because of your many sins, I cast you to the ground; I exposed you to disgrace before kings.

Because of your many sins and the deceitfulness of your trade, you defiled your holy places. I will bring fire out from within you, and it will devour you. I will turn you to ashes in your land before everyone who sees you.
Everyone among the nations who knows you will grieve over you, because you have come to destruction and will never exist again.
Concerning Sidon. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, set your face against Sidon and prophesy against it.

And you shall say: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Look, I am against you, Sidon, and I will be glorified in you. You will know that I am the Lord when I carry out judgments in you and show myself holy in you.
I will send death upon you and blood into your streets. The wounded will fall within you; they will surround you with swords, and they will know that I am the Lord.
There will no longer be a bitter prickle or a painful thorn for the house of Israel from any of those around them who treated them with contempt. And they will know that I am Adonai the Lord.

Thus says Adonai the Lord: I will gather the house of Israel from the nations among which they were scattered, and I will show myself holy among them before the nations and peoples. They will live in their own land, which I gave to my servant Jacob.

They will live in it with confidence, build houses, and plant vineyards. They will live with confidence when I execute judgment upon all those around them who treated them with contempt. And they will know that I am the Lord their God and the God of their fathers.
Concerning Egypt and Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians.
In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians. Prophesy against him and against all Egypt.
Speak and say: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Look, I am against you, Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians, you great dragon who sits among the rivers and says, ‘These rivers are mine, and I made them.’
I will put a hook in your jaws and make the fish of your river cling to your wings. I will bring your rivers out from within you, and all the fish of your river will cling to your wings.

I will cast you down swiftly, swiftly, along with all the fish of your river. You will fall upon the open field and will not be gathered or collected again, for I have given you as food to the beasts of the earth and the birds of heaven.
And all you inhabitants of Egypt will know that I am the Lord, because you were a reed staff to the house of Israel.
When they leaned on you, you passed through their hands; and when any hand grasped you, and when they leaned on you, you shattered and broke all their backs.
Therefore thus says the Lord God: “Look, I am bringing a sword against you, and I will destroy both people and animals from among you.”
The land of Egypt shall become a place of destruction and ruin, and they shall know that I am the Lord, because you said, ‘These rivers are mine, and I made them.’
Therefore, behold, I am against you and against all your rivers. I shall give the land of Egypt over to ruin, the sword, and destruction, from Migdol and Syene to the borders of Ethiopia.
No human foot shall pass through it, nor shall an animal’s hoof pass through it, and it shall remain uninhabited for forty years.

I shall make its land a place of destruction among ruined lands, and its cities shall lie devastated among ruined cities for forty years. I shall scatter Egypt among the nations and disperse them through the provinces.
For thus says the Lord God: After forty years I shall gather the Egyptians from the nations among whom they were scattered.
I shall bring back the captive Egyptians and settle them in the land of Pathros, the land from which they came. There they shall be a kingdom more wretched than all other kingdoms.
It shall be the lowliest and shall no longer exalt itself above the nations. I shall make them few in number, so that they do not become numerous among the nations.
They shall no longer be a source of hope for the house of Israel, a reminder of its lawlessness in following their hearts. And they shall know that I am Adonai, the Lord.
In the twenty-seventh year, on the first day of the first month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made his army labor greatly against Tyre. Every head became bald, and every shoulder was rubbed bare. Yet neither he nor his army received any wages from Tyre for the service they performed for me there.

Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I shall give Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon the land of Egypt. He shall take away its multitude, seize its spoil, and plunder its goods, and this shall be the wages of his army.
In return for the labor with which he served me at Tyre, I have given him the land of Egypt for all that they did for me, thus says the Lord God.
On that day a horn shall spring up for the whole house of Israel, and I shall give you an open mouth among them. And they shall know that I am the Lord.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says Adonai, the Lord God: Alas, alas for the day!
For the day of the Lord is near, a day of clouds, for the end of the nations has arrived.
The sword shall come upon Egypt, and there shall be turmoil in the regions of Ethiopia. The wounded shall fall in Egypt, its multitude shall be taken away, and its foundations shall be overthrown.
Persians, Cretans, Lydians, Libyans, all the mixed peoples, and those of the children of my covenant who are there shall be slaughtered by the sword.
Thus says Adonai the Lord: “The supports of Egypt will collapse, and the pride of its strength will fall. From Migdol to Syene they will fall within it by the sword,” says Adonai the Lord.
They shall be laid waste among devastated lands, and their cities shall be among ruined cities.
They shall know that I am the Lord when I set fire to Egypt and all its helpers are shattered.
On that day messengers shall go out from my presence in haste to destroy the vain hope of the Ethiopians. There shall be turmoil among them on the day of Egypt, for behold, it has arrived.
Thus says the Lord God: I shall destroy the multitude of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
He and his people with him, evildoers among the nations, shall be sent to destroy the land. They shall draw their swords against Egypt, and the land shall be filled with the wounded.
I shall turn their rivers into dry land and deliver the land into the hands of the wicked. I shall destroy the land and all that fills it by the hands of foreigners, for I, the Lord, have spoken.

Thus says the Lord God: I will destroy the abominations and put an end to the nobles of Memphis and the rulers in the land of Egypt, and they will exist no longer. I will cast terror over the land of Egypt.
I will destroy the land of Pathros, set fire to Tanis, and exact vengeance on the people of Diospolis.
I will pour out my wrath on Sais, the stronghold of Egypt, and destroy the multitude of Memphis.
I will set fire to Egypt, and Sais will be thrown into great turmoil. The city of Diospolis will be torn apart, and waters will gush forth.
The young men of Heliopolis and Bubastis will fall by the sword, and their women will be led into captivity.
Day will grow dark in Tahpanhes when I shatter the scepter of Egypt's rule there. The pride of its strength will perish there, a cloud will cover it, and its daughters will be led into captivity.
I will execute judgments in Egypt, and they will know that I am the Lord.
In the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, I have broken the arms of Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Look, they will no longer be bandaged for healing, nor will medicines be applied to them so that they might grow strong enough to hold a sword in his hand.
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Look, I am against Pharaoh, king of Egypt. I will break his mighty arms, covered with sinews and cartilage, and make the sword fall from his hand.
I will scatter Egypt among the nations and disperse its people throughout the lands.
I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and place my sword in his hands. He will bring it against the land of Egypt, seize its spoil, and take its plunder.

I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, and Pharaoh's arms will fail. They will know that I am the Lord when I place my sword in the hands of the king of Babylon and stretch it out over the land of Egypt.
I will scatter Egypt among the nations and disperse its people throughout the lands, and all the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord.
In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, say to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and to his forces: Whom have you likened yourself to in your pride?
Look, Assyria was like a cypress in Lebanon, with beautiful shoots, dense branches, and great height. Its top was among the clouds.
Water nourished it; the deep waters made it grow tall. It brought its rivers around its plantations and spread its dense growth among all the trees of the field.
Therefore its height rose above all the trees of the field. Its branches spread, and its shoots grew tall because of the abundant waters as it spread out.
All the birds of heaven nested in its shoots, and all the wild animals of the field gave birth beneath its branches. All the multitudes of the nations lived under its shade.
It was beautiful in its height because of the length of its branches, for its roots were in abundant waters.
The [?], junipers, and cypresses in the garden of God did not equal its shoots. The cedars and plane trees did not resemble its branches. No tree in the garden of God resembled it in beauty,
because of its forest-thick branches. All the trees in God's garden of delight envied it.
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Because you grew great in height, and your tops reached the clouds, and I saw your pride,
I handed you over into the hands of the ruler of the nations, and they brought him to destruction.

Foreigners, ruthless men from the nations, uprooted him and destroyed him. They cast him down on the mountains, and his branches fell into every valley. His boughs were broken across all the plains of the earth. All the nations [?] came out from his shade and cut him down.
When it fell, it became a resting place for all the birds of heaven, and all the wild animals came to its branches.

This was so that no water-nourished trees would again become proud of their greatness, or stretch their tops into the clouds, or stand in their pride like him who drank water. They were all handed over to the same death, to the depths of the earth, among the human beings who go down into the pit.

Thus says the Lord God: On the day when he went down to the underworld, the depths mourned over him. I held back his rivers and stopped the abundant waters. Lebanon grieved over him, and all the trees of the plain languished because of him.

At the sound of his downfall, the nations shook, when I brought him down to the underworld with those who descend into the pit. All the trees of delight, the choicest and most beautiful trees of Lebanon, which were nourished by water, comforted him in the depths below.
For they went down with him to the underworld, among those wounded by the sword. His offspring, who had lived under his shade, were destroyed in the midst of their lives.

Whom did you resemble in strength, glory, and greatness among the trees of delight? Descend and go down with your trees of delight into the depths of the earth, among the uncircumcised who lie with those wounded by the sword. So it is with Pharaoh and the entire multitude of his forces, says the Lord God.
In the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, take up a lament over Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians, and say to him: You became a lion among the nations, and you resembled a dragon in the sea. You struggled through your rivers, muddied the waters with your hoof, and trampled your rivers underfoot.
Thus says the Lord God: I will surround you with my nets, with an assembly of many armies, and bring you up with my hook.
I will lay you out on the earth, and the plains will be filled with you. I will bring down upon you all the birds of heaven and satisfy all the beasts of the earth with you.
I will put your flesh upon the mountains and fill the valleys with your blood.
And the earth will drink from your spoil, from your abundance upon the mountains; I will fill the valleys with you.
When you are extinguished, I will veil the heavens and darken their stars. I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon will not give its light.
I will darken all the lights above you and bring darkness upon you, says the Lord God.
I will anger the hearts of many nations when I bring your captives among the nations, into a land you do not know.
Many nations will grieve over you, and their kings will be utterly terrified when my sword flashes before their faces, expecting their own downfall from the day of your downfall.
For thus says the Lord God: The sword of the king of the Babylonians will come upon you.
With the sword of giants I will bring down your forces. All the ruthless men of the nations will come and destroy the pride of the Egyptians, and all their forces will be shattered.
I will destroy all their livestock beside the abundant waters. No human foot will muddy them, and no animal's hoof will trample them.
Then their waters will become still, and their rivers will flow like oil, says Adonai the Lord.
When I give Egypt over to destruction, and the land is laid waste with all that fills it, when I scatter all its inhabitants from it, they will know that I am the Lord.
These are lamentations, and they shall lament it; the daughters of the nations shall lament it. Over Egypt and over all its army they shall lament it, says the Lord GOD.
And in the twelfth year, in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, raise a lament over the army of Egypt, and the nations shall bring her daughters, the dead, down into the depths of the earth,
to those who descend into the pit. From the waters of beauty, descend and lie among the uncircumcised, in the midst of the wounded.
They shall fall by the sword with her, and all her army shall come to rest.
And the mighty ones shall say to you: Come, descend into the deepest depths! For whom were you better than? Descend and rest among the uncircumcised, in the midst of those wounded by the sword.
There is Assyria and all its company, all of them wounded.

There its grave was placed in the depths of the pit, and its company was around its tombs. All the wounded fell by the sword, those who made their graves at the bottom of the pits. And its company was around its graves, all of them wounded, fallen by the sword, who spread their terror over the land of the living.

There is Elam and all its army around its grave, all of them wounded, fallen by the sword. They descended uncircumcised into the depths of the earth, those who spread their terror in the land of the living, and they received their torments with those who descend into the pit,
in the midst of the wounded.

There were placed Meshech and Tubal and all their armies around its grave, all its wounded, all of them uncircumcised, wounded and fallen by the sword, who spread their terror over the land of the living.

And they did not lie with the giants who fell in ancient times, who descended into the underworld with their weapons of war. Their lawless deeds were laid upon their bones, because they terrified the giants during their lifetime.
And you shall be shattered among the uncircumcised and shall lie in the midst of those wounded by the sword.
There are Edom, its kings, and all its rulers, who surrendered their strength to the blows of the sword. They too lay with the wounded, with those who descended into the pit.

There are all the rulers of the north and all those commanders of Assyria who descended wounded. Despite the terror inspired by their strength, they lay in shame, uncircumcised, with those wounded by swords, and bore their torments with those who descended into the pit.
Pharaoh shall see them and be comforted over all their army. Pharaoh’s men are wounded by the sword, and all his army, says the Lord GOD.
For he spread his terror in the land of the living, and he shall lie among the uncircumcised who were wounded by the sword—Pharaoh and all his multitude with him, says the Lord GOD.
To the sons of Jacob
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, speak to the sons of your people and say to them: If I bring a sword upon a land, and the peoples of the land take a man from among themselves and appoint him as a watchman,
If he sees a sword coming against the land, he shall blow the trumpet and warn the people.
and someone hears the sound of the trumpet but does not take warning, and the sword comes and takes him, his blood shall be upon his own head.
For he heard the sound of the trumpet and did not take warning; his blood shall be upon himself. But the one who took warning saved his own life.

And if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not signal with the trumpet, and the people do not take warning, and the sword comes and takes one of them, that person was taken because of his own lawlessness, but I shall require his blood from the watchman’s hand.
And you, son of man, I have appointed you as a watchman for the house of Israel. You shall hear the words of my mouth and warn them on my behalf.

When I say to the sinner, ‘You shall surely die,’ and you do not speak to warn the wicked man to turn from his way, that lawless man shall die in his lawlessness, but I shall require his blood from your hands.
But if you warn the wicked man beforehand about his way, so that he may turn from it, and he does not turn from his way, he shall die in his wickedness, but you shall save your own life.
And you, son of man, say to the house of Israel: This is what you have said, and you say, ‘Our errors and our lawless deeds are upon us, and we are wasting away in them. How then can we live?’

Say to them: As I live, says Adonai the Lord, I do not desire the death of the wicked, but rather that the wicked turn from his evil way and live. Turn, turn from your evil ways! Why should you die, house of Israel?

And you, son of man, say to the children of your people: The righteousness of the righteous will not save him on the day when he goes astray, and the lawlessness of the lawless will not bring suffering upon him on the day when he turns from all his lawlessness. Nor will the righteous be able to live on the day of his sins.

When I say to the righteous person, “You will surely live,” and he trusts in his righteousness and commits lawlessness, none of his righteous deeds shall be remembered. Instead, he shall die because of the lawlessness he committed.
And when I say to the wicked, ‘You will surely die,’ and he turns from his sins and does what is just and righteous,
and returns the debtor’s pledge and restores what he has seized, and walks in the commandments of life without doing injustice, he will surely live and not die.
Let none of the sins he committed be remembered, for he has done what is just and righteous; through these he will live.
And the children of your people say, ‘The Lord’s way is not right.’ But it is their way that is not right.
When the righteous turns from his righteousness and commits injustices, through these he will die.
And when the sinner turns from his lawlessness and does what is just and righteous, through these he will live.
“Is this what you say: ‘The way of the Lord is not right’? I will judge each of you according to your ways, house of Israel.”
And in the twelfth year of our captivity, in the tenth month, on the fifth day of the month, someone who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me and said, ‘The city has been taken.’
And the hand of the Lord had been upon me in the evening, before he came, and had opened my mouth before he came in the morning. Once my mouth was opened, it was no longer shut again.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:

Son of man, those who live among the ruins of the land of Israel say, ‘Abraham was one man, and he possessed the land. But now we are many, and the land has been given to us as an inheritance. Shall we not inherit it?’
Therefore say to them: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Since you eat with the blood, turn your eyes toward idols, and shed blood, do you wish to inherit the land?
Let this be a sword for you, for you have committed abominations; each of you has defiled his neighbor’s wife. Will you now inherit the land by doing this?

Therefore say to them: Thus says the Lord God: As I live, I, the Lord, swear that those who are among the ruins will fall by the sword, and those who are out in the open country will be given as food to the wild beasts of the wilderness, and those who are within the walls and in [?] I will strike down with death.
And I will make the land a ruin and a place of destruction, and the pride of its strength will perish. The mountains of Israel will be laid waste, so that no one will pass through them.
And they will know that I am the Lord. I will make its land a ruin, and it will be laid waste because of all the abominations they have committed.

And you, son of man: the children of your people go about murmuring about you beside the walls and at the doors of their houses. They say to one another, each man to his brother, “Let us gather and go and hear the messages that have come from the Lord.”

Now they come to you as people gathering for an assembly, and my people sit before you to hear your words, but they do not carry them out, for falsehood is in their mouths, and their hearts follow their own impurity.
And you will be to them like the sound of a sweet-sounding, well-composed song. They will hear your words but will not do them.
And when it comes, they will say, ‘Look, it has arrived!’ They will know that there is a prophet among them.
To the Shepherds of Israel
The word of the Lord came to me and said:

Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel. Prophesy and say to these shepherds: Thus says the Lord God: O shepherds of Israel, do shepherds feed themselves? Should not shepherds feed the flocks?
But look, you consume the milk and clothe yourselves with the wool; you slaughter the fattened animals, but you do not feed my flocks.

You have not strengthened the weak or healed the sick. You have not cared for the afflicted or bandaged the injured. You have not brought back those who strayed or sought those who were lost. You have worn down the strong and prosperous with toil.
And my sheep were scattered because they had no shepherds, and they became food for the wild beasts of the wilderness and were scattered.
And my sheep wandered over every mountain and every high hill, and my sheep were scattered over the whole face of the earth. There was no one to seek them and no one to bring them back.
Therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord.

As I live, says Adonai, the Lord, the Lord, surely, because my sheep became plunder and my sheep were given over as food for the wild beasts of the wilderness because there were no shepherds, and the shepherds did not seek my sheep, but the shepherds fed themselves and did not pasture my sheep—
Therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord.

Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Look, I am against those shepherds, and I will demand my sheep from their hands. I will stop them from pasturing my sheep, and they will no longer pasture them. I will rescue my sheep from their hands, and they will no longer be food for them.
For thus says the Lord, the Lord: Look, I myself will seek my sheep and look after them.

Just as a shepherd seeks his flock on a day when there is cloud and fog among his scattered sheep, so I will seek my sheep and gather them from all the places where they were scattered on a day of cloud and fog.

“I will bring them out from the nations and gather them from the countries. I will bring them into their own land and pasture them on the mountains of Israel, in the valleys, and in every inhabited place in the land.”

I will pasture them in pleasant pastures on the high mountain of Israel, and their sheepfolds will be there. There they will settle, and there they will rest in the comfort of good things, and they will graze in rich pastures on the mountains of Israel.
I will pasture my sheep, and I will give them rest, and they will know that I am the Lord. Thus says the Lord, the Lord.
I will seek the lost and bring back the straying. I will bind up the broken and strengthen the wasted. I will preserve the fat and the strong, and I will pasture them with justice.
And you, my sheep, thus says the Lord, the Lord: Look, I will judge between sheep and sheep, and between ram and ram.
Was it not enough for you to graze the fine pastures first? Yet you also trampled underfoot the forage you left behind, and you drank the clear water and muddied what remained with your feet.
And my sheep grazed on what your feet had trampled and drank the water muddied by your hooves.
Therefore, thus says the Lord, the Lord: Look, I will judge between the rich and the lowly sheep.
Because you jostled and fought with your sides and shoulders, and butted all the lowly ones with your horns and drove them away until my sheep were scattered,
I will rescue my sheep, and they will no longer be plundered. I will judge between ram and ram.
And I will appoint one shepherd over them, my servant David, and he will shepherd them. He will be their shepherd.
And I, the Lord, will be their God, and my servant David will be a ruler among them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
And I will make a covenant of peace with David and destroy the evil beasts from the land. They will live securely in the wilderness and sleep in the forests.
And I will give them a blessing around my mountain, and I will give you rain, and there will be showers of blessing.

And the trees of the field will yield their fruit, and the earth will yield its abundance. They will live securely and peacefully in their land, and they will know that I am the Lord when I break the yoke from their necks and rescue them from the hands of those who enslaved them.
And they will no longer be plunder among the nations, and the beasts of the earth will no longer devour them. They will live securely, and there will be no one to terrify them.
And I will establish a planting of peace for them, and they will no longer waste away from famine in the land, nor will they bear insults from the nations any longer.
And they will know that I, the Lord their God, am with them, and that they, the house of Israel, are my people, says the Lord, the Lord.
And you, my flock, the sheep of my pasture, are human beings, and I am the Lord your God, says the Lord, the Lord.
Concerning the Edomites.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, turn your face toward Mount Seir and prophesy against it.
And say to it: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Look, I am against you, Mount Seir. I will stretch out my hand against you and make you a wilderness, and you will be laid waste.
I will turn your cities into ruins, and you will become a ruin, and you will know that I am the Lord.

Because you maintained an everlasting hostility and treacherously lay in ambush against the house of Israel by the sword in the hands of enemies, in the time of distress, in the time of iniquity at the final end,
therefore, as I live, says the Lord, the Lord, surely you have sinned through bloodshed, and blood will pursue you. The blood you hated—that very blood will pursue you.
I will make Mount Seir a ruin and a wilderness, and I will destroy both people and animals from it.
I will fill the mountains with your wounded. On your hills, in your valleys, and in all your plains, those wounded by the sword will fall within you.
I will make you an everlasting ruin, and your cities will never again be rebuilt, and they will know that I am the Lord.
Because you said, ‘The two nations and the two lands will be mine, and I will possess them,’ even though the Lord was there,
therefore, as I live, says the Lord, the Lord, I will deal with you according to the hostility and jealousy you displayed in hating them. I will make myself known to you when I judge you.
And you will know that I am the Lord. I heard the sound of your blasphemies, for you said, ‘The mountains of Israel are ruins; they have been given to us as food.’
You spoke arrogantly against me with your mouths and proclaimed your words against me, and I heard.
Thus says the Lord, the Lord: To the joy of the whole earth, I will make you a ruin.
Because you treated the inheritance of the house of Israel with contempt when it was destroyed,
I will do the same to you, and you will become a ruin, Mount Seir, and all Edom will perish. And you will know that I am the Lord their God.
Concerning the mountains of Israel.
And you, son of man, prophesy concerning the mountains of Israel and say to the mountains of Israel: Hear the words of the Lord.
Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Because the enemy said against you, ‘Aha, aha! The everlasting ruins have become our possession,’

therefore prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Because you were held in contempt by all the nations around you and became exiles among many nations, the subject of people's talk and the reproach of the nations,

therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the words of Adonai, the Lord. Thus says the Lord, the Lord, to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys, to the devastated ruins and the abandoned cities that became a wasteland and were trampled by the remaining nations around you:

Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Surely I will speak in the fire of my anger against the other nations and against all the Edomites, because they made my land a place of exile for themselves; they contemptuously dishonored people, laying waste through plunder.

Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel and say to the mountains and the hills, to the valleys and the plains: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Look, I have spoken in my jealousy and anger because you have borne the reproach of the nations.
Therefore Adonai, the Lord, says this: I have raised my hand against the nations around [?]; they will bear their own disgrace.
But, mountains of Israel, my people Israel will eat your grapes and your produce, for they look forward to returning.
Look, I will turn toward you, and you will be cultivated and sown.
I will multiply people upon you, the whole house of Israel in its entirety. The cities will be inhabited, and the ruins will be rebuilt.
I will multiply people and animals upon you; they will multiply and increase. I will settle you as in the beginning and do good to you as I did before. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
I will cause people—my people Israel—to possess you. They will inherit you, and you will become their dwelling place, and you will no longer be bereaved of them.
The Lord God says this: Because they said to you, ‘You are a land that devours people, and you have been bereaved of your nation,’
therefore you will no longer devour people, and you will no longer bereave your nation of children, says the Lord God.
The disgrace inflicted by the nations will no longer be upon you, and you will no longer bear the reproaches of the peoples. Your nation will no longer be bereaved of children, says the Lord God.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, the house of Israel lived in their own land and defiled it by their ways, their idols, and their impurities. Their conduct before me was like the impurity of a menstruating woman.
I poured out my wrath upon them because of the blood they shed in the land, and because they defiled it with their idols.
I scattered them among the nations and dispersed them throughout the countries. I judged them according to their ways and their sins.
They entered among the nations, and wherever they went, they defiled my holy name when people said of them, ‘These are the Lord’s people, yet they have left his land.’
I spared them for the sake of my holy name, which the house of Israel had defiled among the nations where they went.

Therefore say to the house of Israel: The Lord God says this: It is not for your sake that I act, house of Israel, but for the sake of my holy name, which you have defiled among the nations where you went.

I will make holy my great name, which was defiled among the nations, which you defiled among them. The nations will know that I am the Lord, says Adonai, the Lord, when I show my holiness through you before their eyes.
I will take you from among the heathen and gather you from all the nations, and I will bring you to your own land.
I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you will be cleansed of all your impurities. I will cleanse you of all your idols.
I will give you a new heart and renew a new spirit within you. I will remove the heart of stone from your bodies and give you a heart of flesh.
I will put my Spirit within you and cause you to walk in my statutes, keep my ordinances, and carry them out.
You will live in the land that I gave to your fathers. You will be my people, and I will be your God.
I will deliver you from all your impurities. I will summon the grain and multiply it, and I will not bring famine upon you.
I will multiply the fruit of the trees and the produce of the fields, so that you will no longer suffer the disgrace of famine among the nations.
You will remember your evil ways and your conduct that was not good, and you will be disgusted by your lawlessness and your abominations.
It is not for your sake that I do this, says the Lord God. Let this be known to you. Be ashamed and abashed because of your ways, house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord God: On the day when I cleanse you from all your lawlessness, the ruins will be rebuilt, and I will make the cities inhabited.
And the devastated land will be cultivated, instead of lying devastated in the sight of everyone who passes by.
And they will say, “The devastated land has become like the garden of delight, and the ruined, devastated, and demolished cities are fortified and inhabited.”
And the nations that remain all around [?] will know that I am the Lord, who rebuilt the ruined places and restored the devastated places. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will do it.
Thus says the Lord God: I will also attend to the house of Israel to do this for them: I will multiply their people like flocks.
Like holy sheep, like the sheep of Jerusalem at their festivals, so the ruined cities will be filled with flocks of people, and they will know that I am the Lord.
On the Resurrection
And the hand of the Lord came upon me, and he brought me out by the Spirit of the Lord and set me in the middle of the plain, which was full of human bones.
And he led me around the bones, and behold, there were very many on the surface of the plain, and they were very dry.
And he said to me, “Son of man, can these bones come to life?” And I said, “Lord God, you know that.”
And he said to me, “Son of man, prophesy over these bones and say to them, ‘Dry bones, hear the words of the Lord.’”
Thus says the Lord God to these bones: Behold, I will bring living breath upon you.
And I will give you sinews, bring flesh upon you, spread skin over you, and put my spirit in you. You will come to life, and you will know that I am the Lord.
And I prophesied as the Lord commanded me. And there was a sound as I prophesied, and behold, there was movement, and bone came together with bone, each at its own joint.
And I looked, and behold, sinews and flesh covered them, and skin spread over them, but there was no breath in them.

And he said to me, “Prophesy, son of man, prophesy to the breath and say to the breath, ‘Thus says the Lord God: Come, breath, from the four winds, and breathe into these dead people, and let them live.’”
And I prophesied as the Lord commanded me, and the breath entered them, and they came to life and stood up on their feet, an exceedingly great multitude.
And the Lord spoke to me and said, “Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel, and they say, ‘Our bones have dried up, our hope has ended, and we are dead.’”
Therefore prophesy and say to them: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Look, I will open your graves and bring you out of your graves, my people, and bring you into the land of Israel.
And you will know that I am the Lord when I open your graves and bring you out of your graves, my people.
And I will put my spirit in you, and you will come to life. I will set you in your land, and you will know that I am the Lord. I have spoken and have done it, says the Lord God.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:

And you, son of man, take a stick for yourself and write on it, “Judah and the children of Israel who are his companions.” Then take a second stick for yourself and write on it, “Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and all the children of Israel who have joined them.”
And join them together so that they are bound into one stick, and it will be in your hand.
And when the children of your people say to you, “Will you not tell us what this means to you?”

You shall say to them, “Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will take the tribe of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribe of Israel who are his companions, and I will add them to the tribe of Judah. They will become one stick, and they will be one in the hand of Judah.”
And the sticks on which you have written shall be in your hand before them.

And you shall say to them, “Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am taking the house of Israel from among the nations into which they have gone. I will gather them from all the nations around them and bring them into the land of Israel.”
And I will make them one nation in my land, on the mountains of Israel, and one ruler will be king over them all. They will no longer be two nations, nor will they be divided into two kingdoms.

They will no longer defile themselves with their idols, their abominations, or any of their ungodliness. I will save them from all their lawless deeds through which they sinned, and I will cleanse them. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
And my servant David will be ruler among them, and they will all have one shepherd, so that they may walk according to my commands and keep my ordinances and carry them out.

And they will live in their land, which I gave to my servant Jacob, where their fathers lived. They and their children and their children's children will live in it forever, and David my servant will be their ruler forever.
And I will establish a covenant of peace with them; it will be an everlasting covenant with them. I will give to them and multiply them, and I will place my sanctuary among them forever.
And my dwelling will be among them, and I will be their God, and they will be my people.
And the nations will know that I am the Lord who sanctified them, when my sanctuaries are among them forever.
Concerning Gog and Magog
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, set your face against Gog, of the land of Magog, the ruler of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal, and prophesy against him.
And say to him: Thus says the Lord God: See, I am against you, ruler of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal.

And I will besiege you and put a bit in your jaws, and I will gather you and all your forces, the horsemen and horses, equipped and fully armed, from many nations, bearing shields, helmets, and swords.
And all these will be with them: Persians, Ethiopians, Libyans, and Lydians, all wearing helmets and bearing shields.
Gomer and all those around him, and the house of Togarmah from the far north and all those around him, and many nations will be with you.
Make preparations; prepare yourself, you and all the assemblies gathered with you, and be a vanguard for me.

After many days he will be prepared; at the end of the appointed times he will come and reach the land that is safe from the sword, gathered from many nations—the land of Israel, which was completely laid waste. It has been gathered from the nations, and they all live in peace.
And you will advance like rain and arrive like a cloud, and you will cover the land, you and all the many nations around you who will be with you.
Thus says the Lord God: On that day, thoughts will fall into your heart, and you will devise evil plans.
And you will say: I will advance against the secure land; I will come against those who are at rest, who live without care, all living in peace in the land, who have neither walls nor bars nor gates.

To seize spoil and plunder their possessions, to lay my hand upon the land that was devastated and is inhabited, and upon the people gathered from many nations, who have acquired possessions and estates and live in the heart of the land.

Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of the Carthaginians and all its towns will say to you: Have you come raiding for plunder? Have you gathered your assemblies to take silver and gold, to carry possessions away as spoil, and to seize great plunder?
Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog: Thus says the Lord God: On that day, when my people Israel live in peace, will you not awaken?
And you will come from your place in the far north, you and many nations with you, all riding horses, with many companies of numerous troops.

And you will advance against my people Israel like a cloud covering the land. This will happen in the last days, and I will bring you against my land so that all the nations may know me when I show myself holy through you before them, Gog.
Thus says the Lord GOD to Gog: Are you the one of whom I spoke in former days through my servants, the prophets of Israel, in those days and years, saying that I would bring you against them?
And on that day, when Gog comes against the land of Israel, says the Lord GOD, my wrath will rise in anger.
In my jealousy, in the fire of my anger, I have spoken: Surely on that day there will be a great earthquake in the land of Israel.

The fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the beasts of the fields, all the creeping creatures of the earth, and all the people on the face of the earth will tremble before me. The mountains will split apart, the valleys will collapse, and every wall in the land will fall.
And I will summon the terror of the sword against him, says the Lord GOD. Each man's sword will be against his brother.
And I will judge him with blood and death, with torrents of rain and hailstones. I will rain fire and sulfur upon him, upon all who are with him, and upon the many nations with him.
And I will show my greatness and holiness; I will be glorified and make myself known before many nations, and they will know that I am the LORD.
And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say: Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am against you, Gog, ruler of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal.
And I will gather you and lead you, bring you out from the far north, and bring you onto the mountains of Israel.
And I will destroy your bow from your left hand and your arrows from your right hand, and I will strike you down

on the mountains of Israel. You will fall, together with all who are with you, and the nations with you will be given as food to birds and every winged creature. I have given you as food to all the beasts of the wilderness.
You will fall on the open plain, for I have spoken, says the Lord GOD.
And I will send fire upon Magog, and the islands will dwell in peace, and they will know that I am the Lord GOD.
And my holy name will be known among my people Israel, and my holy name will no longer be profaned. All the nations of the earth will know that I am the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
Behold, it has arrived, and you will know that it will happen, says the Lord GOD. This is the day of which I spoke.

And the inhabitants of the cities of Israel will go out and burn the weapons: broken spears, broken shields, arrows, fragments of bows, spear shafts, and sword hilts. They will burn them as their fuel for seven years.

They will not take wood from the open country or cut wood from the forests, but will burn the weapons in the fire. They will plunder those who plundered them and rob those who robbed them, says the Lord GOD.

And on that day I will give Gog a renowned burial place in Israel, the graves of those who came from the regions by the sea. They will build around the sides of the valley and bury Gog and all his assembly there, and it will be called Geh, the burial place of Gog.
And the house of Israel will bury them for seven months, so that the land may be cleansed.
All the people of the land will bury them, and the day on which I am glorified will be renowned among them, says the Lord GOD.
And they will appoint men for this very task: to travel throughout the land, bury the remains on the face of the land, and cleanse it after seven months.
Everyone who passes through the land will search, and when someone sees a human bone, he will set up a marker beside it until the buriers bury it in Geh, in the burial place of Gog.
For the city too will be named Burial Place, and the land will be cleansed.

And you, son of man, thus says the Lord God: Say to every bird that flies and to every wild animal of the field, “Gather and come! Gather from every part of the earth to my sacrifice, which I am offering for you, a great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel. Eat flesh and drink blood.”
Eat the flesh of mighty men and drink the blood of the rulers of the earth—rams, bulls, and male goats—for they are all fattened bulls.
And you will eat fat until you are full and drink blood until you are drunk, from the sacrifices that I slaughter for you.
And at my table you will eat your fill of riders and horses, of mighty men and all warriors, says the Lord God.
And I will give you my glory, and all the nations will see the judgment I have carried out and my hand, which I have laid upon them.
And the house of Israel will know that I am the Lord their God, from that day onward.

And all the nations will know that the house of Israel went into captivity because of their sins. Because they dishonored me, I turned my face away from them and handed them over to their enemies, and they all fell by the sword.
Because of their uncleanness and their lawlessness, I did this to them, and my face turned away from them.
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Now I will bring Jacob back from captivity and have mercy on the house of Israel, and I will be zealous for my holy name.
And they will bear their disgrace and the wrongdoing they committed, when I settle them peacefully in their own land, with no one to terrify them.
When I bring them back from the nations and gather them from the lands of the Gentiles, I will be shown to be holy among them before the nations.
And they will know that I am the Lord their God when I appear to them among the nations. I will gather them into their own land and no longer leave any of them anywhere else.
And I will no longer turn my face away from them, because I have poured out my anger upon the house of Israel, says the Lord God.
Concerning the Construction of the Temple

And in the twenty-fifth year of our captivity, in the first month, on the eleventh day of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was taken, on that very day the hand of the Lord came upon me.
And he brought me in a vision of God to the land of Israel and set me on a very high mountain. On it, opposite me, was something like a city built there.
And he brought me inside, and there was a man whose appearance was like shining bronze. In his hand were a builder’s cord and a measuring rod, and he stood at the gate.

And the man said to me, “Have you seen, son of man? Now look with your eyes, listen with your ears, and fix in your mind everything I will show you, for I came here to show it to you. And you must show the house of Israel everything you see.”

And there were open spaces around the temple. In the man’s hand was a measuring rod of six cubits and a handbreadth. He measured the width of the wall, which equaled the rod, and its height, which also equaled the rod.

And he entered through the gate facing east by seven steps. He measured the chambers, six each, with the gate’s archway equal to the rod, and the length of the chamber equal to the rod and its width equal to the rod. The archways between the chambers were six cubits.
And the second chamber equaled the rod in width and equaled the rod in length, and the archway was five cubits.
And the third chamber equaled the rod in length and equaled the rod in width, and the gate’s archway near the gate’s [?] was eight cubits.
And the archways were two cubits, and there were archways of the inner gate.
And the gate's guardrooms faced one another, three on this side and three on that side. All three had the same dimensions, and the archways on this side and that side had the same dimensions.
And he measured the width of the gate’s entrance at ten cubits and the length of the gate at thirteen cubits.
And there was a one-cubit enclosure in front of the chambers, a one-cubit boundary on this side and that side, and the chambers on either side were six cubits each.
And he measured the gate from the wall of one chamber to the wall of the other chamber, twenty-five cubits in width, and there was a doorway opposite a doorway.
And he measured the space of the gate’s archway and its chambers at sixty cubits around the gate.
and the distance across the outer court and the distance across the portico of the inner gate were fifty cubits.

There were recessed windows in the guardrooms and in the porticoes inside the gate of the court, all around; likewise in the other porticoes. There were windows all around, inside and outside, and palm trees on the porticoes on either side.
He brought me into the inner court, and there were halls and columns arranged all around the court—thirty halls among the surrounding columns.
The columns faced the gates, extending along the length of the gates, and the columns around them were below.
He measured the width of the court, from the middle of the outer gate to the middle of the inner gate facing east: one hundred cubits.
He brought me to the north side, and there was a gate facing north in the outer court. He measured its length and width,
and its guardrooms on either side, its portico, its jambs, and its palm trees. Its measurements were the same as those of the gate facing east: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its windows, porticoes, and palm trees were like those of the gate facing east. Seven steps led up to it, and there was a vaulted portico below.
The gate of the inner court faced the north gate, just as with the gate facing east. He measured the court from gate to gate: one hundred cubits.
He brought me to the south side, and there was a gate facing south. He measured it, its guardrooms, its jambs, and its porticoes; they had the same measurements.
Its windows and porticoes all around were like the windows and porticoes of the first gate. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
