It had seven steps, with porticoes inside and palm trees on the jambs on either side.
There was an inner gate opposite the gate of the court facing south. He measured the width of the court from gate to gate on the south side: one hundred cubits.
He brought me into the inner court through the gate facing south, and he measured the south-facing gate; it had the same measurements.
And its guardrooms, archways, and recesses had the same dimensions, and its windows and archways were all around: fifty cubits in length and twenty-five in width.
There were porticoes around it. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide.
Its porticoes were in the outer court, with palm trees on the porticoes, and seven steps led up to it.
He brought me to the gate facing east, and he measured it according to the first measurement:
its guardrooms, its porticoes, and its jambs had the same measurements. It had windows and porticoes all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide.
Its porticoes were in the inner court, with palm trees on the porticoes on either side, and it had seven steps.
He brought me to the gate facing north and measured it according to the same measurement:
its guardrooms, its porticoes, and its jambs. It had windows all around and porticoes. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its porticoes were outside the gate, with palm trees on the porticoes on either side, and it had eight steps.
Its halls, its broad spaces, and its porticoes were opposite the second gate, where they washed the burnt offerings.

In the gate's portico there were two tables on this side and two tables on that side, so that they could slaughter there the burnt offerings, the sin offerings, and the offerings for unintentional sins.

On the south side of the drain for the burnt offerings, at the entrance to the gate facing north, there were two tables facing east; and on the south side of the second gate, opposite the gate's porticoes, there were two tables.

And toward the east were eight tables, four tables on this side and four tables on that side, opposite the south gate. There they shall slaughter the sacrifices and the burnt offerings, in front of the eight tables for burnt offerings.

And the four tables for burnt offerings were of hewn stone, a cubit and a half long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high, so that they could place on them the tools with which they would slaughter the burnt offerings and sacrifices there.
And they shall have carved brackets a handbreadth long all around on the inside, and a roof over the table to shelter it from rain and drought.

And he brought me into the inner courtyard, and there were two chambers within the courtyard: one by the south gate, facing north and opening toward the south, and one by the north gate, facing south and opening toward the north.
And he said to me, “This chamber facing south shall be for the priests who keep watch over the house.”
“And the chamber facing north shall be for the priests who keep watch over the altar. These are the sons of Zadok who, from among the Levites, draw near to serve the Lord.”
And he measured the courtyard: a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide on its four sides. And the altar was in front of the temple.

And he brought me into the porch of the temple and measured the width of the porch: five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other side. The entrance was fourteen cubits wide, and the capitals of the jambs of the porch doorway were three cubits on each side.
And the porch was twenty cubits high and eleven cubits wide. Ten steps led up to it, and there were two pillars, one on either side.
And he brought me into the temple and measured its arch: six cubits in width on one side and six cubits in the length of the arch on the other side.
And the doorway was ten cubits wide, and the capitals of the doorposts were five cubits on each side. And he measured its length, forty cubits, and its width, twenty cubits.
And he entered the inner hall and measured the arch of the entrance, two cubits, and the entrance, six cubits. The capitals of the entrance posts were seven cubits on each side.
And he measured the length of the doorway, forty cubits, and its width, twenty cubits, in front of the temple. And he said to me, “This is the Holy of Holies.”
And he measured the wall of the temple, six cubits, and the width of the side chamber of the house, four cubits, all around.

And from side to side there were thirty-three cubits, twice over, and a space between the walls of the temple, all around the side chambers, so that those who rested on them could look out and never approach the wall of the temple.

And the width of the sides of the upper gate, according to the [?] of the sides of the walls, toward the upper part around the house, so that the house would be spacious above and below; from these they go up to the upper stories, and from the middle stories to the third story.
And the height of the roof of the house all around, with the spaces between the side chambers, was equal to the rod: one space was six cubits.
And the outer wall of the side chamber was five cubits wide.
And the passageways between the side chambers of the house and the chambers were twenty cubits wide, all around the house.
And the doors of the chambers opened onto the passageways, one door toward the north and one door toward the south. The open area providing light for the passageways was five cubits wide all around.
And the partition opposite the [?], on the seaward side of the passage, was seventy cubits in length. The width of the partition's wall was five cubits, and its length was ninety cubits.
And he measured the front of the house, a hundred cubits long; and the recesses, the intervening spaces, and their walls were a hundred cubits long.
And the width of the front of the house and the recesses opposite it was a hundred cubits.
And he measured the length of the space opposite the recesses behind the house, and the recesses on either side: a hundred cubits long.

And the outer temple, the corners, the arches, the stories, and the latticed windows that admitted light around the three [?] for looking out, and the house and the stories adjoining it, were all paneled with wood all around, from the floors to the windows. The windows were opened in three tiers for looking out, likewise from the lower part to the outside.
And over the whole house all around, and over the whole house on every side, inside and outside,
cherubim and palm trees were carved, with one palm tree between the cherubim, and the two cherubim facing each other.
One cherub had a human face on one side of the palm tree and a lion's face on the other side of the palm tree. The whole temple was carved this way all around.
From the floors to the ceilings, cherubim and palm trees were carved.
And the sanctuary and the temple were [?] and opened in a square.

And directly opposite the sanctuary was something that looked like a wooden altar, three cubits high, two cubits long, and two cubits wide. It had horns, and its base and walls were wooden. And he said to me, “This is the table before the Lord.”
And the temple had two doorways, and the sanctuary had two doorways.
Around the two doorways were two leaves for one door and two leaves for the other door.

And there were carvings on them and on the entrances of the temple: cherubim and palm trees carved like the carvings of the sanctuary. And there was fine woodwork directly opposite the arch on the outer side, and concealed windows.
And he measured the stories of the porch on this side and that side, and the sides of the house joined to one another.
And he brought me out into the outer court toward the east, directly opposite the north gate, and led me inside. And there were chambers with five [?] and recesses on the north side.
They were one hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide,
designed after the pattern of the gate of the inner court and after the pattern of the columns around the outer court, arranged opposite one another in three stories.
And opposite the chambers was a passage ten cubits wide and one hundred cubits long. The innermost side of the passage was one cubit, and their doors faced north.

And the passages in the upper stories were likewise arranged, for the columns all around were joined together from below to above, and the partition likewise, and the columns with their surrounds, the partitions, and the piers, because they were in three stories.
And there were no columns like the columns of the chambers. Therefore there were [?] from the lower part and from the middle stories, on the ground side, fifty.
And there was an opening outside, as with the chambers of the outer court that faced directly opposite the chambers on the north, fifty cubits long.
For the length of the chambers facing the outer court was fifty cubits, and they faced each other across the entire hundred cubits.
And the doors of the chambers were at the eastern entrances, so that one could enter through them from the outer court.
Along the window of the first passage on the south side, facing south and opposite the partitions and facing the recesses,
were the chambers and the passages opposite them, matching the dimensions of the chambers along the passage on the north, their length, their width, their exits, their surrounds, and their windows.

And the entrances of the chambers on the north matched the entrances of the chambers on the south and the entrances of the first passages, to let light into the partition of poles, and to go through them toward the east.

And he said to me, “These chambers on the north and these chambers on the south, opposite the open spaces, are the holy chambers where the priests, the sons of Zadok who draw near to the Lord, eat the most holy things. There they shall place the most holy things, the sacrifices, the sin offerings, and the offerings for unintentional sins, because the place is holy.”

“No one shall enter there except the priests. They shall not go out from the holy place into the outer court, so that whenever they draw near, they remain holy. They shall not approach wearing the robes in which they minister, because these are holy. They shall put on other clothing when they approach the people.”
And the measurement of the inner temple was completed. He led me out by the gateway that faced east and measured the shape of the building all around according to its design.
And he came and stood at the southern gate that faced east, and measured five hundred with the measuring rod.
And he turned toward the north and measured five hundred on the north side with the measuring rod.
And he turned toward the sea and measured five hundred on the side facing the sea with the measuring rod.
And he turned toward the south and measured five hundred on the south side with the measuring rod.

And he measured its passageways all around on the four sides with the same measure, and laid it out, together with its surrounding passageways, at five hundred cubits facing east and five hundred cubits in width, to make a separation between the holy places and the walls of the temple structure.
And he brought me to the gate that faced east and led me out through it.
And behold, the glory of the God of Israel was coming from the east, and the sound of the army was like the sound of many voices echoing. The earth shone like lights from the glory all around.

And the vision I was seeing was like the vision I had seen when I went in to anoint the city. The vision of the chariots that I saw was like the vision I had seen by the river Chebar, and I fell on my face.
And the glory of the Lord entered the temple through the gateway that faced east.
And the Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and behold, the temple was filled with the glory of the Lord.
And I stood there, and behold, a voice from the temple was speaking to me, and a man stood beside me.

And he said to me, “Son of man, have you seen the place of my throne and the place where my feet tread, where my name will dwell among the house of Israel forever? The house of Israel shall no longer defile my holy name, neither they nor their leaders, by their prostitution and by the killings of the rulers among them.”

“When I placed my doorposts among their doorposts and my thresholds beside their thresholds, they put up confining walls between me and them. They defiled my holy name by the lawlessness they practiced, and I crushed them in my anger and with slaughter.”
“At least now let them put their prostitution and the killings of their rulers far away from me, and I will dwell among them forever.”
“And you, son of man, show the house of Israel the temple—its appearance, its form, and its design—and they will cease from their sins.”

“And they shall receive their punishments for everything they have done. You shall draw the building and its arrangement, its exits and entrances, and its furnishings. You shall show them all its commands, all its laws, and its ordinances, and write them down before them. They shall keep all my ordinances and commands and carry them out.”
And the plan of the building is on the summit of the mountain, and all its surrounding boundaries are most holy. This is the law of the temple.

These are the measurements of the altar in cubits, each cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth: its hollow base is a cubit deep and a cubit wide, and the rim around its edge is a span all around. This is the height of the altar:

From the bottom of the hollow base to the large ledge, it is two cubits on the inside, and its width is one cubit. From the small ledge to the large ledge, it is four cubits, and its width is one cubit.
And the base was four cubits, and above the base the horns were one cubit.
The main body is twelve cubits by twelve cubits in width, square on its four sides.
The ledge is fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide, equal on all four sides. The enclosing rim surrounding it is half a cubit, and its surrounding border is one cubit. Its steps face east.
The Lord said to me, “Son of man, thus says the Lord God: These are the regulations for the altar on the day it is made, for offering burnt offerings on it and pouring blood against it.
You shall give a young bull from the herd as a sin offering to the Levitical priests who are descendants of Zadok and who approach me to serve me, says the Lord God.
They shall take some of its blood and put it on the altar’s four horns, on the four corners of the ledge, and all around the base. They shall sprinkle it and make atonement.
They shall take the bull of the sin offering, and it shall be burned in the designated place of the temple, outside the sanctuary.
On the second day they shall take two unblemished male goats as a sin offering, and they shall make atonement for the altar just as they made atonement with the bull.
After completing the atonement, they shall offer an unblemished bull from the cattle and an unblemished ram from the flock.
They shall present them before the Lord, and the priests shall sprinkle salt on them and offer them as burnt offerings to the Lord.
For seven days they shall offer one male goat each day as a sin offering. They shall also offer one bull from the cattle and one ram from the flock, both unblemished.
For seven days they shall make atonement for the altar, purify it, and consecrate their hands.
They shall complete these days, and from the eighth day onward the priests shall offer your burnt offerings and your offerings for well-being on the altar. Then I will accept you, says the Lord God.”
He brought me back by the way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, which faced east, and it was shut.
The Lord said to me, “This gate shall remain shut. It shall not be opened, and no one shall pass through it, because the Lord, the God of Israel, will enter through it. It shall remain shut.
For the prince, the ruler, shall sit in it to eat bread before the Lord. He shall enter by way of the gate’s porch and leave by the same way.”
He brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the temple. I looked, and behold, the house of the Lord was filled with the glory of the Lord, and I fell on my face.

The Lord said to me, “Son of man, take to heart, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears everything I will tell you concerning all the regulations of the Lord’s house and all its laws. Take to heart the entrance to the house, all its exits, and all its holy places.
You shall say to the house of Israel, the rebellious house: Thus says the Lord God: Enough of all your lawless deeds, house of Israel!

You bring foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, into my holy places to defile them, while you offer my bread, with fat and blood. You violate my covenant with all your lawless deeds.
You have not kept charge of my holy places, but have appointed them to keep charge of my Holy of Holies.
Therefore thus says the Lord God: No foreign-born person, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in body, shall enter my sanctuary, from among all the foreigners who are in the house of Israel.
But the Levites who departed from me when the people went astray, who strayed from me after their own schemes, shall bear the consequences of their lawlessness.

They shall be ministers in my sanctuary, gatekeepers at the gates of the house and attendants in the temple. They shall slaughter the burnt offerings and sacrifices for the people, and they shall stand before the people to serve them.

Because they served before their idols, and this became a punishment for wrongdoing for the house of Israel, therefore I raised my hand against them, says the Lord God, and they shall bear the consequences of their lawlessness.

They shall not approach me to serve me as priests, nor touch any of the holy things of the Israelites, nor any of my most holy things. They shall bear their disgrace because of the error into which they strayed.
They shall appoint them to keep watch over the house, for all its work and for everything that is done there.

But the Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept charge of my sanctuary when the house of Israel strayed from me, shall approach me to serve me. They shall stand before me to offer me sacrifices, fat, and blood, says the Lord God.
They shall enter my sanctuary, and they shall approach my table to serve me and keep my charge.
When they enter through the gate of the inner court, they shall put on linen robes. They shall not wear wool during their service at the gate of the inner court.
They shall have linen turbans on their heads and linen trousers around their loins, and they shall not wear anything tightly binding.

When they go out to the outer court, to the people, they shall take off the robes in which they minister and put them in the chamber of the sanctuary. They shall put on other robes, so that they do not make the people holy by their robes.
They shall not shave their heads or thin out their hair; they shall keep their heads covered.
None of the priests shall drink wine when they enter the inner court.
They shall not take a widow or a divorced woman as a wife, but virgins from the offspring of the house of Israel. However, they may marry a widow who has been left by a priest.
They shall teach my people to distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the clean and the unclean.

In cases involving bloodshed, they shall stand to examine the matter. They shall uphold my righteous decrees and administer my judgments. They shall keep my laws and my commands at all the festivals, and they shall keep my Sabbaths holy.
They shall not approach a human corpse and become defiled, except that they may become defiled for a father or mother, a son or daughter, a brother, or a sister who has not been given in marriage.
After his purification, he shall count seven days for himself.
On the day he enters the sanctuary of the inner court to minister in the sanctuary, he shall offer an atonement offering, says the Lord God.
They shall have no inheritance, for I am their inheritance. No landed property shall be given to them among the Israelites, for I am their inheritance.
They shall eat the sacrifices, the offerings for sins, and the offerings for unwitting offenses, and every dedicated gift of Israel shall be theirs.

The fruit of everything, the firstborn of all, and the firstfruits of all your produce shall belong to the priests. You shall give the first yield of your produce to the priest, so that a blessing may rest upon your houses.
The priests shall not eat any bird or animal that has died on its own or been torn by wild beasts.

When you allot the land as an inheritance, you shall set apart a sacred offering to the Lord from the land, twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide. It shall be consecrated throughout all its boundaries.
Within it there shall be a square of five hundred by five hundred for the sanctuary, with fifty cubits of open ground all around.
From this measured area, twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in width shall be measured out, and within it shall be the Holy of Holies.
The portion dedicated from the land will belong to the priests who serve in the sanctuary, those who approach to serve the Lord. They will have a place set apart for the house of their sanctuary.
Twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in width shall belong to the Levites who serve in the temple, as a possession consisting of a city for them to live in.
For the city's settlement you shall give five thousand in width and twenty-five thousand in length, alongside the sacred offering. It shall belong to the whole house of Israel.

The ruler shall have land on this side and that side of the sacred offering and the city's settlement, opposite the sacred offering and facing the city's settlement, along the side toward the sea and from the sea toward the east. Its length shall correspond to one of the allotments, from the boundaries on the seaward side, and its width to the boundaries of the land toward the east.

It shall be his possession within Israel, and the rulers of the children of Israel shall no longer oppress my people. The house of Israel shall inherit the land by allotment according to their tribes.
Thus says the Lord God: Enough, you rulers of Israel! Now put away wrongdoing and misery; practice justice and righteousness. Remove oppression from my people, says the Lord God.
You shall have honest balances, an honest measure, and an honest cab as your measure.
The cab shall be the same for giving and receiving. A cab shall be one tenth of a bushel, and the cab shall be one tenth of a bushel. The measure shall be according to the bushel and the artaba.
The weight shall be twenty obols, and twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, and another twenty-five shekels shall make one mina for you.
This shall be the offering you set apart: one sixth of a measure from a bushel of wheat, and one sixth of an artaba from a cor of barley.
The prescribed amount of oil is one sextarius of oil, one tenth of a jar, for ten sextarii make one jar.
And one sheep out of ten sheep shall be offered as gifts from all the tribes of Israel, for sacrifices and burnt offerings, for your atonement and deliverance, says the Lord God.
All the people of the land shall give the firstfruits to the rulers of Israel.

The ruler shall be responsible for the burnt offerings, offerings, and sacrifices at the festivals, new moons, and Sabbaths, at every festival of the house of Israel. He shall present the sin offerings, offerings, burnt offerings, and offerings for deliverance, to make atonement for the house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord God: In the first month, on the first day of the month, you shall take an unblemished bull from the herd to make atonement for the sanctuary.

And the priest will take some of the blood of the sin offering and sprinkle it on the thresholds of the house, on the four corners of the temple, on the altar, and on the thresholds of the gate of the inner court.
You shall do the same on the seventh day of the month for everyone who sins unknowingly and for the children, to make atonement for the house.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall celebrate the Passover festival. For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
And on that day the ruler will offer one bull from the herd as a sin offering for himself, for the house, and for all the people of the land.

During the seven days of the festival, he shall offer burnt offerings to the Lord: seven unblemished bulls and seven unblemished rams each day for seven days, and one male goat each day as a sin offering.
And an offering and prepared fine flour shall be provided for each bull, and prepared bread for each ram, and one sextarius of oil for each loaf.
In the third month, on the fifteenth day of the month, they shall celebrate a festival following the same pattern for seven days, with the same sin offerings, burnt offerings, fine flour, and oil.
Thus says the Lord God: The gate of the inner courtyard that faces east shall remain closed during the six working days, but it shall be opened on the Sabbath and on the day of the new moon.

The prince shall enter through the porch of the outer gate and stand at the threshold of the gate. The priests shall offer his burnt offerings and his peace offerings for him. He shall bow down at the threshold of the gate and then go out, but the gate shall not be closed until evening.
The people of the land shall bow down before the Lord at the entrance of that gate on Sabbaths and at new moons.
The burnt offerings that the prince shall present to the Lord on the Sabbath shall be six lambs without blemish and one ram without blemish.
There shall be a cooked grain offering with the ram, and with the lambs, offerings and gifts according to what he can provide, and a pint of oil for each bread offering.
On the day of the new moon, there shall be one young bull, the offspring of a heifer, without blemish; the six lambs and the ram shall also be without blemish.
There shall be [?] for the bull, and [?] and a grain offering for the ram, and for the lambs as much as he can provide, with oil in proportion to the [?].
When the prince enters, he shall enter through the porch of the gate and go out by the same way through the gate.

And when the people of the land come before the Lord at the festivals, whoever enters by way of the north gate to bow down will leave by way of the south gate, and whoever enters by way of the south gate will leave by way of the north gate. He must not return by way of the gate through which he entered, but must go straight out that way.
And the ruler will be among them: when they enter, he will enter with them, and when they leave, he will leave with them.

At the feasts and assemblies, there shall be a cooked grain offering for the bull, a grain offering for the ram, and for the lambs as much as he can provide, with one pint of oil for each bread offering.

If the prince offers burnt offerings of thanksgiving and voluntary peace offerings to the Lord, the gate that faces east shall be opened for him. He shall offer his burnt offerings and his peace offerings in the same way as he does on the Sabbath. Then he shall go out, and the gates shall be closed after he has gone out.
You shall offer a year-old lamb without blemish as a burnt offering to the Lord every day; you shall offer it every morning.
And with it, morning by morning, a grain offering of one-sixth of a measure and one-third of a sextarius of oil mixed into the fine flour—a grain offering to the Lord, an everlasting ordinance.
They shall continually present the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil. He shall prepare it every morning as a regular burnt offering.
Thus says the Lord God: If the prince gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his sons, it shall belong to his sons as an inherited possession.

If he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall belong to that servant until the year of release, and then it shall return to the prince. But his sons’ inheritance shall remain theirs.

The prince shall not take any of his people’s inheritance by forcing them out. Instead, he shall give his sons an inheritance from his own possessions and his own inheritance, so that none of my people may be scattered from their own dwelling places.
He brought me through the southern gate to the porch of the holy places belonging to the priests, which faced north. There was a place set apart there.

He said to me, “This is the place where the priests shall cook the offerings for unintentional wrongdoing and the offerings for sin. They shall also cook the grain offering there, so that they do not bring them out at all into the outer courtyard and make the people holy.”
He brought me out into the outer courtyard and led me around the four sides of the courtyard. There were courts, one at each of the four sides of the courtyard.
The small court was forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide. All four had the same measurements.
There were porches around all four, with cooking places built beneath the porches all around.
He said to me, “These are the kitchens where the servants of the house shall cook the people’s sacrifices.”

He brought me before the entrance of the temple, and water was coming out from beneath the curtains of the temple toward the east, for the front of the temple faced east. The water flowed from the right side of the temple, on the north, toward the altar.
He brought me out by way of the north gate and led me around by way of the outer gate to the outer gate facing east. And there the water was flowing from the right side.
As the man went out straight ahead, with a measuring line in his hand, he measured a thousand measures and passed through the water. The water was rising.
He measured a thousand measures and passed through the water, and the water reached the thighs. He measured a thousand measures and passed through the water, and the water reached the waist.
He measured a thousand measures along the [?], and he could not cross, because the water had risen like the torrents of a flood, which no one could cross.
He said to me, “Have you seen this, son of man?” Then he turned me around and brought me to the riverbank.
When I returned there, I saw very many trees planted on the riverbank, on both sides.
He said to me, “This water goes out toward the region of the Galileans to the east, descends into Arabia, and reaches the sea, into the waters of its outlet, and it will heal the waters.

Every living animal among those that swarm [?] will live wherever the river comes. There will be very many fish there, because when this water reaches there, it will bring healing. Whatever the river reaches will be made alive and will live.
Fishermen will stand beside it, from En-gedi to En-eglaim. There will be separate places for spreading nets, and its fish will be like the fish of the Great Sea, exceedingly numerous.
At its outlets, at its bends, and where it rises, let the waters not be purified, but let them be given over to salt.

Along the river, on its banks on both sides, every kind of tree bearing food will grow. What surrounds it will not grow old, and its fruit will not fail. It will send forth its fresh growth early, because its waters come out from the sanctuary. Their fruit will be for food, and their growth for healing.
Thus says the Lord God: “These are the boundaries of the inheritance of the land that is to be allotted to the twelve tribes of the children of Israel, with additional portions.
They shall inherit it, each one like his brother, the land that I raised my hand to give to their fathers. That land shall fall to you as an allotted inheritance.
These are the boundaries of the land: on the northern side, from the Great Sea, where it descends and extends to the entrance of Zedad,
and Hamath, Berothah, and Sibraim, between the boundaries of Damascus and the boundaries of Hamath, and the settlements of Enan, which are within the boundaries of Hauran.
These are the boundaries: from the sea to the encampment of Enan, the boundaries of Damascus, and on the northern side toward the north, the boundaries of Hamath. This is the northern boundary.
Facing east, between Hauran and Damascus, between Gilead and the land of Israel, the Jordan forms the boundary toward the eastern sea, along the palm grove. This is the eastern side.
And on the south, southward, from Teman and from the palm grove as far as the waters of Meribah-kadesh, extending to the Great Sea: this is the southern and southward boundary.
And this same portion of the Great Sea forms the boundary as far as opposite the entrance of Hamath, as far as its entrance. These are on the seaward side of Hamath.
You shall divide that land among them and the tribes of Israel.

You shall allot it by lot to yourselves and to the foreigners residing among you who have children among you. They shall be to you like native-born people among the children of Israel. They shall be with you and shall eat from the inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
They shall be in the tribe of foreigners, among the foreigners who are among you. There you shall give them an inheritance,” says the Lord God.

These are the boundaries of the tribes: beginning on the northern side, along the side of the slope that forms the boundary toward the entrance of Hamath, the encampment of Enan, the boundary of Damascus to the north, along the side of the settlement of Hamath. They shall have territory from the eastern side to the seaward side: one portion for Dan.
And along the border of Dan, from the eastern side to the western side, Asher shall have one portion.
And along the border of Asher, from the eastern side to the western side, Naphtali shall have one portion.
And along the border of Naphtali, from the eastern side to the western side, Manasseh shall have one portion.
And along the border of Manasseh, from the eastern side to the western side, Ephraim shall have one portion.
And along the border of Ephraim, from the eastern side to the western side, Reuben shall have one portion.
And along the border of Reuben, from the eastern side to the western side, Judah shall have one portion.

And along the border of Judah, from the eastern side to the western side, there shall be a dedicated offering of land, twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in width, like one of the allotted portions extending from the eastern side to the western side; and the sanctuary shall be in their midst.
The offering that they shall dedicate to the Lord shall be twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in width.

The offering of holy land for the priests shall be twenty-five thousand in length along the southern side, ten thousand in width along the western side, ten thousand in width along the east, and twenty-five thousand in length along the northern side; and the boundary of the sanctuary shall be in their midst.
It shall be for the consecrated priests, the sons of Zadok, who keep the charge of the Lord’s house, who did not go astray when the children of Israel went astray, as the Levites did.
And they shall be given an offering from the offering of the land, a most holy portion along the border of the Levites.
And the Levites’ portion, which shall adjoin the priests’ border, shall be twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in width.
None of it shall be sold or measured out, nor shall the firstfruits of the land be taken away, for it is holy to the Lord.
But the remaining five thousand in width, alongside the twenty-five thousand, shall be an outer enclosure for the city, for residences and its open grounds; and the city shall be in its midst.

And these are its dimensions: on the northern side, four thousand five hundred; on the southern side, four thousand five hundred; on the eastern side, four thousand five hundred; and on the western side, four thousand five hundred.
And the city’s open ground shall be two hundred fifty to the north, two hundred fifty to the south, two hundred fifty to the east, and two hundred fifty to the west.

And the remaining length, adjoining the sacred firstfruits offering, shall be ten thousand to the east and ten thousand to the west. These shall be firstfruits dedicated as holy, and their produce shall provide food for the worker of the city.
And the workers of the city, from all the tribes of Israel, will cultivate it.
And the entire offering shall be twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand, a square. You shall separate the sacred offering from the city’s residential area.

And what remains shall belong to the ruler, on either side of the sacred offering and the city’s site: opposite its twenty-five thousand in length, as far as the boundary on the eastern side, and on the western side, opposite its twenty-five thousand, as far as the boundary on the western side, adjoining the ruler’s allotment. And the sacred offering and the sanctuary of the temple shall be in its midst.

And the area between the Levites’ inheritance and the city’s residential area shall belong to the rulers; and what lies between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin shall belong to the ruler.
And for the remaining tribes, from the eastern side to the western side, Benjamin shall have one portion.
And along the border of Benjamin, from the eastern side to the western side, Simeon shall have one portion.
And along the border of Simeon, from the eastern side to the western side, Issachar shall have one portion.
And along the borders of Issachar, from the eastern side to the seaward side, one portion for Zebulun.
And along the borders of Zebulun, from the eastern side to the seaward side, one portion for Gad.
And from the borders of Gad toward the south, its boundary shall be at Teman, and from the waters of Rabboth Kadesh, one inheritance as far as the Great Sea.
This is the land that you shall divide by lot among the tribes of Israel, and these are their portions, says the Lord God.
And these are the entrances and exits of the city: on the northern side, four thousand five hundred by measure.
And the gates of the city shall bear the names of the tribes of Israel: three gates on the northern side, one gate for Reuben, one gate for Judah, and one gate for Levi.
And on the eastern side, four thousand five hundred by measure, with three gates: one gate of Joseph, one gate of Benjamin, and one gate of Dan.
And on the southern side, four thousand five hundred by measure, and three gates: one gate for Simeon, one gate for Issachar, and one gate for Zebulun.
And on the seaward side, four thousand five hundred by measure, and three gates: one gate for Gad, one gate for Asher, and one gate for Naphtali.
The total distance around it shall be eighteen thousand, and from that time onward the name of the city shall be “The Lord Is There.”
